question: Some people believe that older school students should study a large number of subjects, but others think that they should study only that subject that they need. Discuss both views and give your own opinion?
content:
The importance of having an education system with varied subjects remains controversial, with some arguing that learning various subjects ought to be encouraged among high schoolers so as to build a well-rounded perspective. Meanwhile, there are those who point out the necessity of studying the subject of their specialty. Personally, the latter idea seems far favorable because of conveniences it offers.

Studying a wide range of subjects is able to provide learners with a comprehensive understanding of the surrounding world. Focusing only on one subject, however efficient, does not guarantee that a high schooler can be equipped with what requires to be a responsible and open-minded adult, whereas the study of varied subjects might do so. This is the reason why education still requires students to study a dozen subjects, say, a student, who is preparing to become a doctor, might still need to be introduced to other subjects - for instance, mathematics and sociology. The former is needed as modern medicine relies heavily on data, machines and computers, whereas the necessity of understanding cultural differences and public health problems justifies the latter.

Nevertheless, I remain convinced that it is learning one subject at a time that benefits the most. This is often because switching between subjects too frequently might appear as energy-and-time-consuming. An older student, while preparing for multiple national exams and university admissions, might struggle to focus on many domains, which is why doing one might save them energy and let them fully immerse themselves in the subject, boosting the efficiency of progress. The more time a person spends on one thing, the better outcomes they achieve. Career-oriented education is the epitome in this regard, as statistics tend to show that there is a higher rate of graduates pursuing further education or landing a job after studying in these institutions.

The enhancement of a career path is another factor to be considered important. As students grow older, it is no longer an option to explore different subjects, which is mainly because it may already be time to be more consistent and determined about their career. At this age, gaining as much knowledge as possible in one domain is what is regarded as the most important, while this speciliziation helps them to be competitive in the job market if they wish to find a job after graduation. There is always a higher chance of someone, who excels in their profession, to obtain employment than those who divided their education on a number of areas. An engineering student who concentrates largely on learning geometry and physics is more likely to become competent than those who dividing equal attention among many unrelated subjects, for instance.

In conclusion, an intention toward a broader outlook is one of the reasons why the focus on many subjects is intrinsic, yet this is overshadowed by what specializing in one subject can provide. This type of education is time-and-energy-saving, while it also produces well-prepared students for employment and further education.

question: Some people believe learning language is more effective in small classes others believe the number of people doesn't matter. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
content:
It is widely suggested that the language can be mastered efficiently if it is conducted in small number groups, whereas some claim that learning a language is not about the number of learners in the class, but rather methods used. Personally, the latter idea seems far rational as what is vital is materials, behaviour and age of learners.

From one perspective, it might seem reasonable to suggest that one can improve their language skills in small-numbered classes. During traditional classrooms - where it is common to have from a dozen to twenty students sitting in one room - people might be stripped off an opportunity of expressing their ideas, as these classes need to be, particularly, ‘chaotic’. In other words, A student might feel overwhelmed and even stressed because of the pressure shown in the classroom, and even they can assume that an incorrect answer might represent them as low-achiever, a state many are emberresed to be positioned in.It is not uncommon that students at schools often struggle to voice their opinions,for instance, in classrooms of twenty to thirty students, since they tend to think that a person, who is asking a lot, may be shown as a straggler, especially language-oriented classrooms.

Nevertheless, I am still of the opinion that student partication is not about classroom sizes, which is easily overshadowed by a number of factors. One of the most contributing factors to the growth of language skills is the approach teachers opt to conduct their classes. There may be a teacher, who is aware of their students’ flaws and strong points, and then there is someone who just occurs to teach rather robotically without consideration of aforementioned aspects of learners. Naturally, the former might experience a greater outcome in the language acquasition, while students with the latter find it challenging to move forward in the progress, for example.

Another factor that accelerates language acquisition is the quality of textbooks used during lessons. The more a student is exposed to authentic and well-designed materials, the more progression one is likely to demonstrate, since ineffective learning materials can just confuse a learner rather than guide them towards the improvement of language abilities. Conversely, if choosen methodically improving textbook that integrate real-life contexts, varied exercises, and progressive difficulty can substantially aid to the improvement of language learning. It is not surprising that there are cases when students study for months and still might not achieve profciency band advancement.

In conclusion, although younger language learners might feel overwhelmed by the sheer size of the group due to the psychological barriers to participation, language acquisition is more about other factors. I feel that the teaching methodology and the quality of materials are greater contributors to it.

question: Many people stay in contact with others with the help of the technology. Do the disadvantages outweigh its advantages?
content:
Our life has been profoundly transformed by the influence of technology, and it even facilitates interaction regardless of geographical and language barriers. However, face-to-face communication has a personal touch, a unique trait that digital devices cannot replace, but I believe that the benefits online communication has to offer are still far more favorable than the disadvantages.

One of the most compelling features of face-to-face communication is the absence of physical presence that makes online communication feel emotionally distant. Conversations tend to feel more genuine, spontaneous, and emotionally rich when people talk to each other face-to-face, which builds a closer relationship and mutual understanding, whereas video calls seem not to deliver these traits of interaction. There are still thousands of people who gravitate towards having important meetings offline rather than just connecting through video or audio calls.

Having said that, there are several outstanding perks of online communication. One is that it brings people together despite their locations or time zone. It is incredible that we can connect with our loved ones, who might be living thousands of kilometres away in another continent, at the touch of the screen, an experience that was impossible just a few decades ago. Families, for instance, can check in on their children studying abroad and stay updated on events happening on both sides. This proves especially useful in cases of emergencies and crises, when a family member passes away, or when an accident occurs, or when someone falls seriously ill.

Another remarkable benefit that AI generated models can only offer is the ability to communicate regardless of linguistic differences. Recently, a number of phone companies have integrated AI assistants into their software, meaning that people no longer have to hire third-party taranslators, making business calls significantly cheaper and easier. These models can translate languages without delays in real time and offer privacy, resulting in an experience that feels more private where individuals can express themselves freely. Moreover, some platforms have also introduced real-time chat translators which convert text from any language into a preferred language or the language set as default by the other party;for instance, such a development has been adopted by Telegram - a messenger platform - which has gained a widespread popularity due to such updates. Businessmen and online influencers appear to enjoy these features , as they can maintain contact with others without language gaps.

In conclusion, it is true that video calls are unable to replicate the personal connection of face-to-face conversations. However, advanced technologies provide a hassle-free communication without having to worry about language difficulties or where we are.

question: Many people work from home using modern technology today. Some people think that only the workers benefit from this and not the employer. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
Indisputably, technology has profoundly transformed our lives, and it is argued that there are those who take a benefit of it working remotely, enjoying a number of opportunities like freedom of timetable and reduced distraction. However, this is considered to be a negative development for employers, since it presents hidden costs - reduced managerial control and confidentiality risks. While I admit that remote work carries genuine merit, I also believe that there are far detrimental effects for employers.

It is undeniable that working remotely largely benefits employees in various ways, one of which is uncontrolled timetable. Traditionally, employees are required to arrive at work and leave it at assigned time - if this rule is broken, they are given usually financial fines - which can become monotonous and draining over time. Working 9/5 clearly puts familial cohesion at risk, as workers tend to allocate fewer time for their family members, leading to self-isolation and weakening of family bonds. However, those who work from home do not come across these challenges, as the responsibility of managing their time can entirely rely on themselves, which is why it is becoming more and more common for new generation to gravitate towards this type of work for clear benefits it has to offer, for instance.

Another area where telecommuting shows a significant advantage is how it can be less distracting. In offices, especially in open plan ones, it might get extremely with all those noises of keyboard sounds, printing machines, and talking colleagues. Oftentimes, it is difficult for individuals to concentrate on, especially when they are up to important tasks or in a rush, which is why preference toward working from home may prove to be reasonable, since they can fully embrace quite moments of work without external disturbances.

Nevertheless, I assert that what makes remote work so unfavorable for employers is weakened monitoring mechanisms. Indeed, managers may find it utterly difficult to monitor their workers and control their actions when they operate remotely from their homes: demanding video serveilance can be an impossible feat in this case. This decline in managerial supervision might result in declined efficiency and quality of the workforce, say, workers might not complete tasks on time. Moreover, managers tend to give immediate feedback in conventional work settings, which may not work in remote work, leading to poor decision making during projects, and even underperformance can remain undetected for long periods without proper supervision.

Further, there is data security which is something not talked so often as far as remote work is considered. Since personal networks and devices provide poor safety as opposed to those used in companies, there is potentially higher exposure to cyber threats, where confidential documents can be stolen with ease. If an employee uses their personal laptop, it may have no antivirus, or shared access with family members: any of these becomes a door into company data. Furthermore, there might happen unpredicted errors in the exchange of information between those who are working remotely. Recently, there has been an occasion when a worker from Paramount Pictures - a famous animation studio - sent an entire movie, which is called Aang The Last Airbender, to a wrong email, eventually causing unofficial leakage of this movie online, an action that led to huge financial strain.

In conclusion, while remote work demonstrates notable advantages for employees, where flexible scheduling and fewer interruptions are the main ones, the company can suffer greatly too. This is mainly because of weakened managerial supervision and data safety issues that greatly reduce productivity.

question: More and more universities are replacing face-to-face teaching with online courses. Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
content:
Offline lessons are being increasingly displaced by online ones across a large number of educational institutions for genuine merits — for instance, reduction in operating costs and increased opportunities for overseas students. However, this shift in the education system seems to carry detrimental effects on what traditional institutions should represent.

There are tangible benefits of running online lessons rather than providing in-person ones, one of which is a significant minimization of expenses. Offline lessons oftentimes encompass expenses such as teachers' pay, space, and facility costs that should cater for students at the highest standard — these tend to require a great deal of funding which universities must cover through students' tuition fees, resulting in higher fees when a good quality of education is aimed for. However, lessons available online might cut these expenses, while this leads to relatively reasonable tuition fees, making acquiring a degree accessible for students of different backgrounds.

Another notable change in education due to online courses is the opportunity provided for students regardless of geographical barriers. In other words, those who live in other countries might also enjoy high-quality lessons from renowned institutions — Stanford University, Yale University, and Oxford University, to name a few — at a reasonable cost and without difficulties. As for the latter, students frequently confront culture shock, financial challenges, and family problems while attempting to study abroad, but all of these can be remedied via online lessons, a chance that completely tailors to learners' needs.

Nonetheless, such an education system cannot be fully justified, since the value of education can be lost. Conventionally, there is student-teacher communication and an exchange of ideas between students in universities, which ensures academic competence. Moreover, students are able to get immediate feedback from their professors during in-person lectures and ask questions. These intrinsic interactions might become absent during courses conducted on online platforms — for instance, on Zoom or YouTube — which is why a number of institutions still run offline courses despite having state-of-the-art technologies.

In conclusion, although both students and universities greatly benefit from online lessons, I regard them as a rather undesirable change. This is because the values offered by traditional courses are irreplaceable by their counterparts.

question: It has been suggested that everyone in the world wants to own a car, a TV, and a fridge. Do you think the disadvantages of such a development outweigh the advantages?
content:
The intention towards purchasing household appliances such as a car, a TV, and a fridge has increased at an unprecedented rate due to their practical applications in the household. However, there are detrimental effects of this trend - especially in the environmental and social terms - which is why its downsides are far greater than its benefits.

Admittedly, universal access to these goods would bring genuine improvements in the standards of living. Massive ownership of cars can shorten daily commutes significantly, thereby reducing reliance on public transport and making everyday-commutes of workers quite convenient, and even in terms of logistics cars can help to transport goods across distances that would otherwise be prohibitive, while fridges can preserve food, reducing waste and improving nutrition where fresh produce is scarce. Meanwhile, TVs can prove intrinsic in terms of educational value, as children in the area with limited access to schools and libraries, serving as an open and free source of education. These are not trivial benefits, and they can explain why ownership of such items are widely desired.

Nevertheless, the environmental cost of this would be severe. Cars are among the leading contributors to the increase of carbon emissions around the world, and a world in which every household owns one would place an enormous strain on fossil fuel reserves and accelerate climate change, leading to serious environmental issues at a rate that existing renewable infrastructure is not equipped to offset. The mass production of TVs and fridges at a global scale may demand vast quantities of rare earth materials and generate significant industrial waste, most of which often end up in landfill sites in developing nations. The cumulative ecological damage of mass consumer ownership, extended to every corner of the world, would be difficult to reverse.

Beyond the environment, the cultural consequences deserve attention. The homogenization of consumer aspirations - largely driven by television advertising - risks eroding of locally distinct ways of life, resulting in the loss of unique cultural differences among nations where multinational companies would benefit more than communities it reaches. Furthermore, this can push lower-income families into debt or divert spending from education and healthcare, eventually reinforcing rather than reducing inequality.

In conclusion, although the need to purchase these appliances may offer real practical advantages, the environmental degradation and social disruption that accompany their universal adoption represent far too undesirable consequences. Hence, in my view, this trend is unfavourable as a whole and outweighs its benefits.

question: As major cities continue to grow, so do their problems What are the problems this may cause?
content:
What are the solution for these problems?

There is a view that the urban expansion might result in the rise of specific urban-related issues - especially in terms of the environment and infrastructure. However, there are a number of measurements to combat, encompassing the introduction of sustainable developments and better urban planning schemes.

The urban sprawl might severely damage nearby flora and fauna. As city borders continue to extent, it subtly starts to cover green areas in the outskirts and countryside. Over time, the whole area turns out to be a huge concrete jungle, resulting in the loss of the wild-life and greenery, a loss that can be detrimental also to the well-being of urban dwellers. The loss of green places might result in the loss of some rare wild animal species, as seen in some western cities where the result of city expansion have contributed to the disappearance of animal species that were endangered or unique to these ecosystems.

Beyond environment, infrastructure issues deserve attention. A drastic increase in urban borders might bring about challenges in distribution of city facilities fairly around the region, which is mainly because the more area a city covers, the more facilities the government should confer, meaning that the government might confront financial constraints in the provision of basic urban facilities such as schools, kindergartens, hospitals and commercial areas, while urban planning of these amenities might prove to be difficult due to the vast area the city covers. This can, moreover, give rise to commuting difficulties where city residents might spend more time than usual, where carbon levels can also surge within urban areas.

Nevertheless, aforementioned problems are able to be mitigated with the proper measures. The most effective solution can lie in urban greening strategies. These often involve the construction of eco-friendly schemes, such as vertical gardens, rooftop gardens, and urban forests, all of which, however fiscally demanding, help to reduce the urban heat island effect, improve air quality, support biodiversity, and boost residents’ mental health.

Smart city-planning and decentralisation might yield notable outcomes, while the city expansion is taking place. Instead of simply stretching outwards and building housing areas, the consideration of the division of the city into well-planned zones ought to be carried out, which can reduce commuting problems in metropolises. Facilities - such as educational institutions, parks, and shopping areas - can be distributed evenly across different areas of the city rather than concentrated in one area, a change that can bring increase residential cohesion and unity, since these traits are often absent in urban communities.

In conclusion, rapid urban expansion places considerable strain on the natural environment and the infrastructure. These, however, can be remedied through green urban and adequate urban planning initiatives.

question: In many countries, traditional food is being replaced by international fast food. Some people claim that this has negative effects on both families and society. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

Personally, this ideas seems to carry heavy weight because of the ways it damages the quality of food, homogenizes the food culture, and leads to the loss of family recipes.

The dominance of the fast food is particularly problematic in terms of the reduction of the quality of food. To put in simpler words, this sort of food is oftentimes produced in ways that are harmful from a health standpoint, for a number of inorganic and semi-ready products are used in the process of making, which tend to include chemicals that can damage the health or contain a high concentration of fat and ultra-processed additives. There are cases when people were reported with obesity, kidney failure, or heart attacks mainly due to the excessive consumption of fast food.

The homogenization of food also deserves attention in this regard. The strong dominance of fast food comes with a problem of losing cultural uniqueness across global cuisines, which is mainly because of the declined practises of traditional recipes, as more and more people chose to dine out rather than cook at home. This increase preference to this particular food is attributable to several factors of the fast food that appeal to many - such as, affordability, availability, convenience, and the taste that feels universally appealing to almost everyone. The success of fast food chains, therefore, has accelerated at an unprecedented level for the past few years.

The final argument in the topic is reduced familial traditions, but not the least. There are thousands of family recipes that have been practised for centuries, a sort of tradition that have grown to have an intrinsic role in the family relationship. Little moments shared during the process of cooking a certain dish and sharing it around the table is what most of the people tend to reminisce after years pass, while this practise also helps to strengthen children-parent bonds. In Uzbek families, for instance, plov is not cooked for not only eating, but also for bringing family members together. On special occasions - holidays, birthdays, and wedding parties - everyone gets together around the table, and while adults cook, they teach their young how to cook, cut carrots, or a special spice they add to make the dish more flavorsome. Over time, these moments become unique family memories, whereas losing them may weaken emotional connections between families.

In conclusion, fast food places a serious threat to global health, while it leads to poorer-quality meals and reduces family closeness. These effects of fast food, hence, make its massive spread less favorable, which is why I believe stepping away can be a step forward.

question: There have been many inventions in human history (for example, the wheel) some people think the most important invention is the internet. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?
content:

However, I partly disagree with this opinion, while I believe that there are several benefits of the internet in our daily life.

The internet offers great advantages in our daily life. One is that it has made our communication much easier, because now people can get in touch with their close ones regardless of the time and geographical location. With a single touch of a screen, they are able to share important updates in their life or just have casual chats, which is important because it helps people to be closer to their family and friends, as early communication tended to be done mainly through letters, which sometimes would take weeks or months to reach a desired person. However, contemporary people can not only just communicate, but also share videos, files, audio messages, making modern communication more interesting and convenient.

Having said that, I still believe that there are more fundamental inventions throughout human history. The wheel is one of them, which has helped humans significantly to develop as a species. Since the creation of the wheel, human civilization has moved forward noticeably, as it improved how we transported goods around the world, as transporting food and cargo could take a long period of time before it. Likewise, the wheel gave rise to horse-drawn carriages and even to modern vehicles, while it accelerated how knowledge was spread in the past as well as the development of nations. For example, a new invention created in Europe could be seen in use in Asia after only a week or month, which was mainly due to merchants who brought these inventions to their country.

In conclusion, we have seen a rise of many great inventions in history, and the internet is one of the most appreciated ones in modern culture. However, I am still of the opinion that other inventions like the wheel have played an equally important role in our history, if not more.

question: Some people think that historical objects should be returned to the country they originally came from. Others believe they should stay in the museums where they are now. To what extent do you agree or disagree that they should be returned?
content:
It is widely argued that returning looted artefacts to their home country should be carried out. I partially agree with this opinion.

Admittedly, one of the most important reasons for keeping artefacts in their place is that large museums have the expertise and resources to preserve looted artefacts. These artefacts oftentimes prove to be fragile, which is why they should be managed carefully and kept in special archival repositories, or else they can be easily damaged over time. Large museums, such as The Louvre and The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, have the experience of dealing with such objects, and they provide facilities to safeguard them. Such facilities include climate-control technology, safety measures, and restoration capabilities.

Having said that, I still remain convinced that looted artefacts should be returned to their country of origin. This is mainly because they rightfully belong to these countries, and the reason why they happen to be in other countries in the first place is that they were looted during wars or the colonial era. This is the most common scenario with African countries, since they have experienced several wars so far. Consequently, their historical artefacts with cultural significance are now in some European museums, but returning them can help to restore nations' identities.

In conclusion, while it is true that some large museums have the necessary skills and technology to save looted artefacts for a long time, I believe that countries should be given the right to take their historical artefacts back.

question: Directors of large companies earn much higher salaries than ordinary workers. Some people say that this is necessary, while others believe it is unfair. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
content:
There is a debate that a relatively higher salary is oftentimes given to company executives in many companies, and some argue that this is important. However, there are those who assume that such a pay system is unjust. Personally, I believe that the former view is more convincing.

Granted, some people think that the pay system where executives receive significantly more than ordinary workers is an act of injustice. Sometimes, we can see in some companies that the actual contribution of ordinary workers is noticeably greater than that of company directors. This results in a bigger salary gap between them, which can dissatisfy employees, and they can lose their interest in their workplaces. Subsequently, there can be an increased employee turnover, which results in an instability in the company’s performance. This is negative in front of investors, who can help to improve and expand the company in the long term.

However, I agree with supporters of the opinion that the salary of company leaders should be higher. This is mainly because important decisions are often made by company leaders, and therefore, they usually have a greater responsibility within the company. For example, an important strategic decision regarding the financial situation or a production process is made by leaders, and they have more experience and knowledge about the company’s goals and ambitions. A simple mistake made by an executive can lead to a bankcruptcy, which results in the loss of employment among thousands of workers and those who depend on this company. Moreover, ordinary workers do not often concern themselves about the performance, future, fiscal decisions of the company, and everything in between out of their own responsibility, whereas the leader should be flexible and concerned about every aspect of its company.

In conclusion, a fair pay system is indeed important when the contribution of workers is greater than that of leaders, but in most cases a relatively higher salary of leaders is reasonable. Leaders are often under more pressure and take a greater responsibility in the company.

question: Some experts say for road safety cyclists should pass a test before being allowed on public roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

The arguments towards not introducing such a scheme are reasonable, since cycling is just a simple form of mobility. In many communities, cycling is considered a normal day-to-day mode of transport. Cyclists in these places often go strolling or travel short distances either to relax or to get to their shopping destination, whereas bikes are not a main form of transport. The idea of introducing a testing system, therefore, might seem like a limitation of freedom - a simple daily enjoyment.

Although the argument above is flawless, I still assume that the increased urbanisation and the ever-increasing population in cities might actually demand that cyclists pass a test. Cities are now home to many modes of transport - for example, buses, taxis, metros and private cars - so it is important to be able to orientate and mobilize in such heavy traffic areas. Without the right driving and cycling rules, there might be confusion and unwanted accidents among drivers and cyclists, so the need for cycling assessment rises.

Moreover, there is the complexity of road systems. Compared to the last 10 or 15 years, roads are much more complicated at present: they need to be much bigger, equipped with different kinds of traffic lights, and there are even multi-lane roundabouts. For a cyclist, getting around on such road infrastructure might be real trouble, often leading to road collisions and ending up at the wrong destination. In fact, riding a bicycle has moved from a simple relaxing activity to a mandatory type of transportation now, where those who choose to be eco-friendly - and healthy in their own way - travel by bike. Some European countries, for instance, have already put such testing campaigns into practice, and therefore** do not permit cyclists without a licence on roads, an act that reduced driver-and-cyclist collisions by a great percentage.

In conclusion, although in the past cycling was regarded as a sort of pastime, now it has become a real form of transportation in urban regions. Cyclists should take a test so as to improve road safety because of the sophisticated road infrastructure and the volume of transport.

question: People living in the 21st century have a better quality of life than people who lived in previous times. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
There has been a noticeable leap forward in people’s lifestyles and the opportunities offered to them from the 20th to the 21st century, and we are believed to have a better standard of living now than people in the previous century. There is no denying the technological advancements this century has to offer, yet I believe that the standard of living has failed to improve.

The 21st century has undoubtedly been the era of technology, as we have moved rapidly from old box TVs to watching our favourite series and movies on digital platforms. All areas of life, for example entertainment, infrastructure, household appliances and education, to name a few, have seen changes, thereby improving our experience of life. Most of these new technologies have made it possible to move away from repetitive tasks and focus on what entertains and makes us happy, allowing more time for hobbies. A simple innovation such as the internet, for instance, has completely changed our lives. People around the world can now connect and communicate regardless of geographical and cultural boundaries, and it is also easier to find information online, so the internet alone seems to be the greatest improvement contemporary people have experienced.

Despite this, technological advancement cannot overshadow the current global issues, which suggests that people are no better off today than they were in the past. International conflicts have risen in the 2020s, such as the war between Ukraine and Russia or the one in Palestine, the results of which have extended to countries far in the west and east, affecting both the social and economic aspects of their lives. The influence of these conflicts can be seen, for example, in the rising cost of fuel, as ongoing conflicts are occurring around the primary points of fuel export. People are finding it more difficult to survive in such harsh economic conditions while trying to support their families.

Another reason why life has been no better in this century is constant bad news and information overload. The rise of the internet has allowed information to spread at an unprecedented level, so people are always exposed to traumatic news from all around the world, leaving a sense that the world is falling apart. Moreover, this so-called marvellous invention of the 21st century has caused a new disease known as information overload. Social media platforms, messages from friends and family members, and news are constantly being fed into our brains, yet we were never meant to consume such a large amount of information, leading to daily issues such as exhaustion, anxiety, mental fatigue, and memory and recall problems.

Beyond global wars and psychological effects, there are environmental problems that we have to deal with at present. The 21st century has witnessed some of the most severe environmental degradation in history, if not the most severe, and its impact is felt on every continent. Of course, a large amount of resources is needed to mitigate these issues that are worsening our planet and health, although very little attention is given to them. Cities are suffering from poor air quality, as the ever-rising number of cars on the roads and continuously working factories release more and more toxic gases, not to mention the animal extinction that we humans have brought about.

In conclusion, one might understandably get excited about how advanced our lives are compared to the past, yet the severity of ongoing conflicts between nations, constant exposure to negative news, information overload causing mental problems, and environmental damage give people reasons to experience this century negatively.

To conclude, being aware of the purpose of traditions and using it to befriend with locals are the right ways, and people should do so. However, getting mixed with them and doing what exactly do other nations should not be the aim, as it may result in several negative consequences.

question: News plays a crucial role in many people's lives and is influential. Why is this the case? Is it a positive or negative development?
content:
The advent of advanced communication technologies has transformed the way we consume news, yet its influence on shaping societal behavior and individual decisions remains profound. While news keeps businesspeople informed and has the potential to guide public actions, I believe it contributes positively to societal development.

There are several reasons why news is so impactful in our daily lives. First, despite the overwhelming amount of information available online, news outlets remain crucial in keeping people informed about developments in various fields, such as business, academia, and science. Authentic news sources allow businesspeople to stay updated on market conditions, enabling them to make informed decisions, such as entering new markets. Furthermore, news significantly affects consumer behavior, particularly through advertising. When news channels introduce new products, they influence consumer choices, leading to more informed financial decisions. Additionally, the role of news in public health is undeniable, as seen during the COVID-19 pandemic. The widespread coverage of the virus helped inform citizens about its symptoms and preventive measures, thereby playing a crucial role in public safety.

In my opinion, news plays a fundamental role in improving society. Investigative journalism, for example, holds corporations and powerful entities accountable for their actions, thereby preventing corruption and abuse of power. This watchdog function ensures that those in power are aware of the scrutiny they face, which can lead to more ethical behavior. News also has the power to unite communities by highlighting shared concerns, celebrations, and events. Such coverage can foster a sense of unity, encouraging collective action on issues of common interest. Moreover, an informed citizenry is essential for a functioning democracy. By keeping the public informed about local, national, and global events, news empowers citizens to make well-informed decisions. This is vital for public discourse and ensures that voters have access to relevant information when participating in democratic processes.

In conclusion, news is a vital component of society due to its ability to inform, guide, and unite the public. It plays a crucial role in enabling informed decision-making, both at an individual and societal level. As such, news contributes positively to societal development by ensuring accountability and fostering an informed and engaged populace.

question: A large amount of the food produced in the world is wasted. Why is this happening, and what can be done to reduce food waste?
content:
the diversity of produce in recent years ahs grown up significantly, and people do not consume much of the food produced, this can be blamed down to uncontrolled supervision of factories and consumers' desire for perfect looking food while this issue can be dealt with the number of precautions.

one factor that drives food waste can be a whole host of factors beyond the grower's control. before the produce has been transported to markets, they usually go through a number of steps in which they might be considered unsuitable for consumption. this can be connected to issues that stem from weather, pest, disease, low market prices or high labor costs, and these factors contribute to food left in the field. another vital key why people just throw away food can be the intention for perfect fruits or vegetables. people in this century has become obsessed with perfectionism in a way that they want everything to look just as they wanted. as a result, much of the food in supermarkets left unpurchased even if they are edible.

the issue is not easy to solve; however, with the right approach it cam be mitigated. one potential solution to on farm losses is to have groups and organizations collect leftover crops to distribute to food banks, where they are stored and repurposed in either ways that leftover food is fed on livestock or recycled and made into fertilizers. this approach could reduce the amount of food being thrown away in a few years, but this requires extra sectors taking the responsibility and expense to work on the project. However, this is not issue as there are already come countries implementing this to prevent food losses. Furthermore, relaxing cosmetic quality standards for fruits and vegetables could prevent waste on farms on a large scale. Still, it would require consumers to overlook blemishes, bruises or imperfect produce so that there is a market for growers. However, informing people to ignore such imperfections can be challenging as they already tend to assume that food with imperfections is not edible, and certainly this can take some time.

To conclude, food losses are not only driven from consumer choices but also a number of reasons such as pests, diseases and market low prices, and the issue can be dealt with the right initiatives such as informing public and legislating accountable entities.

question: Some people believe that protecting the environment is the responsibility of every individual, while others think governments and large companies should take responsibility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: Some people believe that parents should decide how children spend their free time, while others think children should be free to choose their own activities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
Channeling the leisure time of children to beneficial activities can help to boost their skills, and there is a view that this should be managed by their parents whereas I side with those who support the view that giving the independence to choose their pursuits in free time can be vital.

There are those who believe that it is a responsibility of a parent to select the free time activities instead of their children. it is often true due to the fact that children are not well aware of the surrounding environment, and giving the freedom to them can lead to several negative effects. As most of the children in their early childhood tend to have the unrealistic opinions how the world is built, and their interest in everything can become a barrier to do a particular activity for the long run. Moreover, some children tend to switch between leisure time activities often since they can get easily bored of the activity. this can pose a difficulty to grow their performance and full potential. However, their parents can have a wider opinion what can benefit to their juveniles, and direct them into a more promising future.

on the other hand, as young individuals children also should be allowed to take the independence to decide their pastimes. this can have some potential benefits to them as they could have more insights who they are, and what they are capable of. If this choice is done by their parents, children , for example, may never get a chance to fully discover their self as a individual. The true nature and talents of a child can be left hidden forever. In addition, when the choice is done by juveniles, this can seem to them more suitable, and give some interest actually to take the activity seriously. Put simply, being forced by someone for a child can be dissatisfying, and the freedom of choice can make them more satisfied with the decision, and have motivation to continue doing it.

In my opinion, whether the choice is taken by a parent or a child, the interest of the child should be taken into account, and forcing someone to do what they dislike is morally wrong. However, giving much independence to a child can be also foolish as they tend to have oftentimes a changing mind what actually appeals to them. Therefore, it is not an easy task to decide whose accountability, but above mentioned factors should not be ignored.

To conclude, while the strict management of the pastime of children can benefit to them by their parents, it also seems justifiable to free children to make their own choices. However, it seems to me that the real accountability can be the cooperation of both sides having taken into consideration that the parent can make a wise decision, and a child can go for its interest.

question: Some people think that competition at school and at work is the best way to encourage people to achieve more, while others believe that cooperation is more effective. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
What mostly drive people to create innovations is usually competition or cooperation, and there are those who support the importance of competition at academic institutions, and workplaces. However, there are also supporters of collaboration over competing. Personally, I assert that the combination of both is more efficient.

On one side, the supporters of competition often point to the fact that it can drive people to put their limits out, and aim for more. it is often argued that when there is, for instance, at workplace competition among employees for the promotion, the workers can be unusually creative and managed in terms of tasks and time. Therefore, most of western companies set a competitive environment for their employees to achieve outstanding outcomes. As for school setting, the same can also be applied as the competitive surrounding is effective for students. Students, especially primary school pupils, yearn to out-stand among their peers, and be regarded as the top student of the class. In fact, the result of which is that it can open a place for improvement, and learn more than what the school curricula requires. Thus, the competition in both above mentioned settings can be efficient as it is a key to innovative and hardworking aspects.

that said, there are also who feel that the ideology of implying competitive environment is unjustifiable, and the important one is cooperation. they usually highlight the importance of delegation of responsibility rather than taking all the burden one's shoulder. Since, when there is wise distribution of tasks in a team, the result might be more promising, and , in fact, it can also be attained in a shorter span of time. Another major benefit of collaboration is that it gives a place for idea sharing. For instance, Students can exchange the challenges, innovations, sources, and feelings that they are facing, which certainly is limited in a competitive environment. it also helps to build to soft skills such as team skills and confidence. Hence, the need for cooperation is more reasonable.

In my opinion, although both arguments can be justifiable, the best approach to success in any setting is to mix both of the collaboration and the competition. the key to do so can be create, for example, teams which function using both qualities at the same time. With this, the outcome can be more effective.

To conclude, while the competition urges a sense of leaving others behind, and striving for success out of their limit, the collaboration aims to a friendly-setting, resulting in exchanging ideas, and building team skills. However, I assume that Companies and schools should create a setting which supports the competition and the collaboration.

question: Some people think that watching foreign films and TV programmes benefits a country's culture, while others believe that films and programmes should be produced locally. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
It is noted that The introduction of foreign movies and TV programmes can benefit to the culture of a country although there are those who feel that these means of media should be produced in a local region which is a better solution. Personally, I believe that both views have their own advantages, and the best approach is to balance foreign media and local one.

There are several keys areas that benefit from watching foreign media, and one major upside of which is that it encourages the cultural exchange of ideas and traditions. When people are exposed to a foreign culture simply through movies, it can help them to understand better their culture. In fact, many people, for example, in my country come to know about Indian culture especially by just consuming their movies, which are quite well-known in Uzbekistan. Additionally, Foreign movies tend to be of higher quality than those in a local region, which makes people enjoy movies with better storytelling, acting as well as visual effects. The good example can be movies from Marvel studios that are popular all around the world.

Having said that, as much as arguments for broadcasting foreign movies are justifiable, there are also counterarguments to do so. One major risk stems from it is that it effects to the culture of people, resulting in the loss of cultural identity. When these kinds of movies are usually aired on TV, the way how individuals in the movie behave and talk, what they wear, drink, and eat can be woven into the watchers, which greatly causes the homogenization. It is often true when youngsters attempt to imitate their favorite celebrities, taking these actors cultural identity. Moreover, when foreign movies are introduced into a particular region, it creates a competitive environment which could be challenging to deal with for local movie studios. It eventually leads to both economic reduction in a film industry and the growth of this industry. Therefore, Foreign movies can pose a potential threat to local movie industries, and often referred to avoid importing them.

From my perspective, Foreign movies are a key factor to widen horizons of common people, and enhance their world awareness. Although there are some areas that they drive obstacles for local industries, they should be ignored, and welcomed widely. I also exsert that the competition foreign movies bring about is in reality can be a driving force to develop local film industry.

In conclusion, While there are strong arguments represented towards importing foreign media to a region, these often are challenged by the threats it carries to the local culture and film industry. However, I feel that these movies should be welcomed by the local society as it helps to improve the quality of movies produced locally.

question: Some people think that governments should ban dangerous sports such as skydiving and skiing. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
there is a view that the government should restrict the engagement in extreme sports like sky diving and skiing, as they pose a potential threat to the sportsmen. However, I firmly believe that these sports are essential in two factors.

Opponents of legislating a ban on extreme sports usually point out the fact that These types of sports are detrimental as far as the safety and overall well-being of athletes are concerned. it is true that extreme sports often require physical exertion and travelling to dangerous places or participation in dangerous events. Therefore, they pose more injuries and fatalities than traditional sports, oftentimes resulting in even death. For example, one article suggests that there have been the death accounts among athletes those engaging in skydiving over the last years, as even one risky judgment during the activity could lead to fatal conditions. Thus, supporters of it argue that outlawing extreme sports would likely prevent such accidents.

Having said that there are also counterarguments to enforcing a ban on extreme sports. One reason is to do with the advertisement industry. Big name sports companies tend to promote their products with broadcasting the involvement in extreme sports to create unique product promotions, or to provoke an insight that their products can help to achieve results shown in advertisements. RedBull and Esports are the real life examples that employ such advertising in their product advertisements, capturing the attention of the audience. It can aim to sell the feeling than just a drink or clothes products.

Furthermore, it is also note-worthy that extreme sports provide mental health benefits. Involvement in such activities can result in the production of hormones such as dopamine, endorphins, and serotonin which are the source of adrenaline rush. These hormones can push participants outside their comfort zone and are often done in conjunction with adventure travel, resulting in the overall improvement in soft skills such as the boost in self confidence, physical fitness, increased balance, and more importantly fear management skills, which can work out very well for athletes prior to competitions.

In conclusion, although prohibiting the engagement in extreme sports seems justifiable taken into account the risk it involves, I completely disagree with the view as it is a key factor to enhance mental and physical preparation of the athlete, and even is used in the advertisement industry. me

question: Some people say that the quality of a product is the most important factor in increasing sales, while others think that marketing and design matter more. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: Because of globalisation, countries are becoming more and more alike, and travelling to discover new things is becoming less attractive. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
content:
Recently travelling to other countries to discover new things has decreased significantly as the world now is alike one big village. While Globalization is contributing highly to this shift, disadvantages that stem from this is far greater than advantages.

Most of the countries have converged with one another due to several reasons while The globalization is a main trigger of this cause. As trade, travel, and communication has become easier, people have more commonplace in clothing fashion, food choices, ideas. People now can have the abundance of product choices, and can order them online or buy in any traditional market. To give an example, after visa to different countries have been legislated in my country ( Uzbekistan), we can travel to any country. This mass exposure to other cultures has resulted in the change of fashion, turning out the whole traditional fashion in Uzbekistan.

There are a number of benefits that homogenization has to offer. One major benefit is to do with the education. With travelling to other countries to continue their studies or to study abroad, people may benefit to their own culture. They can have an opportunity to acquire high quality of overseas education, and after graduating, they can become skilled employees to their own culture to enhance the economy. Furthermore, Homogenization can facilitate the exchange of ideas, recourses and knowledge. When people from different backgrounds and societies become more similar, it becomes easier to collaborate across borders and communicate. This can lead to innovation in diverse fields such as technology, art, and science as individuals from varying cultures bring their perspectives and expertise to the table.

Having said that, convergence with other cultures also has its disadvantages. one primary drawback is the loss of cultural identity and diversity. As countries become a unified place, there is a risk of traditional practices, languages, and customs being overshadowed or even lost. This can lead to the loss of individual and collective identity, making all places across the world look similar boring places. Unique cultural expressions can disappear or be replaced by mainstream and globalized ones. Therefore, taking into account this trend, the disadvantages of homogenization bare a greater risk than advantages.

In conclusion, Globalization can be considered as the primary driver of homogenization while enhanced education systems and creating a space for exchange of recourses are the main benefits of it. However, these upsides are easily overtaken by the risk of cultural uniqueness being eliminated.

question: Some people think that everyone in the world should speak one global language. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
content:
Due to geographical borders there are a huge number of languages around the world, and many are of the opinion that inventing one lingua franca ought to be carried out. While this shift brings about many straightforward solutions to problems, disadvantages of it are far greater.

One of the main advantages of legislating one world language is that it promotes greater communication between different languages. When people from different backgrounds speak a universal language, this condition dismantles communication barriers and offers a gateway to understanding one another's culture as the language is the focal point of cultural identity.

Furthermore, thanks to globalization the ratio of international trade and businesses has increased significantly, in turn, requiring more communication between between individuals from diverse countries. Thus, A global language can facilitate international trade, and eliminate communication barriers which can result in the economic growth.

On the other hand, a global lingua franca can pose a threat to minority languages. As above mentioned case with the globalization, some individuals assume that whether they are capable of speaking , for instance English- the most used language now in the world, can determine success and opportunities for their financial state and career. This shift in the local language carriers may result in the loss of some languages, and this is detrimental as an extinct language means the loss of a unique culture.

To conclude, as many strong points as one world language can have such as paving a way for communication between different cultures and opportunities for greater international trade, it mainly speaks to the disadvantageous side as the takeover of minority languages by global ones is the main issue.

question: Some people think that manufacturers and supermarkets are responsible for reducing the amount of packaging on goods. Others believe that it is the consumers' responsibility to avoid buying over-packaged products. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
there is a view that all the accountable authorities like manufacturers and supermarkets for producing goods should decrease the level of packaging while there are also those believing that it is customers who are responsible for not purchasing over packaged goods. Personally, I support the former view as it is easier to pose a legislation on responsible entities rather than individuals.

Supporters of the view that Companies and sellers should bear the responsibility of minimizing the amount of packaging mostly point out to the fact that these authorities have the most control over how the product is manufactured or distributed to markets. They should impose changes in the supply chain. For example, they can choose eco-friendly strategies to package their products such as using biodegradable materials or ones that are recyclable. This , in turn, can bring a solution to environmental issues such as waste pollution or plastic pollution since most of the packaging materials are made of plastic which deteriorates in a slow rate in nature. Moreover, Governments can also provide incentives to encourage this shift in companies.

On the other hand, it is undeniable that consumer choices have more impact on companies. Therefore, customers may influence companies and supermarkets in such a way that they should avoid buying over-packaged products. They can do so by using reusable bags or buying products that have the least amount of packaging. Eventually, this change in consumer choice can effect companies to turn their faces to above mentioned environmentally friendly ways to package things. For reliance on companies might be too slow or insufficient.

From my perspective, the most practical solution is to control supply chain of companies by imposing regulations on how they produce goods and distribute to sellers as the accountability always lies on the shoulders of those manufacturing goods. Furthermore, this measurement should be taken by local or international entities to manage actions of companies whether they are following their corporate responsibility to lessen environmental pollution.

In conclusion, the reduction in packaging can be carried out by both companies and retail sellers, and individuals. However, it is advisable that all companies should be controlled by official entities as these companies bear the most power over the product packaging and distribution.

question: More and more people today choose to eat organic food. Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative development?

question: Nowadays, more and more information is stored on the internet rather than in books. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
content:
With the advent of technologies, there has been a significant shift in preserving knowledge, turning back from traditional practices such as books to the internet. Although this has several outstanding drawbacks, I assert that this kind of trend can speak mainly to the advantageous side.

Cloud storage of data can trigger several problems to users, and one potential drawback occurs especially when the user does not have access to the internet. When the business of a user heavily relies on time and remotely stored information, internet failure leads to costly downtime. Furthermore, if the individual has a poor connection to the internet, it may require a long span of time in order to access cloud data.

Additionally, there are privacy concerns which can be detrimental. When employing such a way of preserving information, users have to sing in websites showing their personal information, and this practice can come with a negative in a way that the hackers can use this info to do illegal activities, or even in the worst scenario it can result in unwanted cyber crime.

As much as modern practice of storing data poses threats to users, there are several beneficial sides that, in my view, can easily outstand. For example, this sort of shift requires less storage area. To put simply, keeping knowledge on books needs a large amount of space and demands the construction of facilities that offer such an opportunity. However, when the information is converted into digital one, a single computer can handle a huge proportion of data that could require a library to preserve.

Another benefit that speaks to cloud storage is data redundancy. It can be a critical feature in cloud storage as it provides the data being able to replicated across users for safety and accessibility. This redundancy is designed to safeguard against data loss, ensuring that data remains accessible during hardware failures or other disruptions. To take as an example - when the company fails to preserve the data safely or malfunction occurs in the software, the data can be accessed through other means such as using other servers.

To conclude, cloud storage can provide a user's personal information to hackers, it necessitates uninterrupted access at all times; however, these are easily outstripped by features like data redundancy and less storage capacity.

question: Some people believe that a person's age is the main factor that influences their buying behaviour. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
Shopping is one of the most engaged activities all across the globe, and there is a view that consumer buying behaviour is more triggered by their age group than any other factors. However, I strongly disagree with this view as the psychological and family factors drive more this notion.

I contend that the age of consumers effects greatly to their daily shopping as every individual purchases products according to their needs. Every age group goes for different types of products. While the younger generation prefers to purchase more luxurious items such as cars, clothing and accessory, The elderly focuses on more buying what they need in a daily basis like things that are necessary to live such as medicine and food.

However, this does not mean that all people's shopping attitudes are caused by this type of perception. The psychological factors such as motivation can contribute on a larger scale. Motives towards shopping often compel shoppers to seek satisfaction in their shopping, where individuals are driven by a range of needs, from basic psychological requirements like food and shelter to higher-level desires for esteem and self-actualization. When a particular need becomes pressing, it triggers a motivational state that directs the behaviour toward fulfilling that necessity. Take as an example skincare products - appealing to consumers' desire for youthful skin by emphasizing its anti-aging benefits.

People are also influenced by those around them as social beings. From the early days, our preferences are shaped by our family, friends, and social circles, eventually forming our buying behaviour. Moreover, The youth are greatly influenced what is known as - peer pressure - that most of the time not often determines their shopping, aiming at aligning with their social groups. In the case of family shopping habits, in a traditional household, for instance, the mother and father may have differing preferences in purchasing at the same time while that for children also varies significantly, but the family needs outstripping those leads to a commonly agreed decision. These purchases exerts to varying degrees of influence in shopping decision-making among different members of a family.

In conclusion, Shopping habits are not solely forced by the age group of consumers, as psychological factors and surroundings of people greatly impact on their decision-making.

content:

question: Fossil fuels are the main source of energy around the world. However, people are being encouraged to use alternative energy sources such as wind energy, solar energy and so on. Do you think this is a positive or negative development ?
content:
While fossil fuels are the primary source of energy in many countries, some people call for the switch to renewable energy sources. This shift towards alternative energy sources is generally favorable, but not without its drawbacks. As far as I am concerned, this is a change for the better.

On the one side, It is admittable that the widespread adoption of renewable energy comes with its disadvantages. First of all, This trend can require substantial initial investment, not to mention expenses incurred from maintenance and hiring experts. All this adds further weight to the case against the movement towards replenishable energy sources. Another concern over the use of alternative energy is a rise in the unemployment. Once have generated and distributed such energy, many people in this field can render jobless, resulting in an economic unbalance.

Having said that, abandoning fossil fuel-based energy forms could be justifiable as renewable energy sources may have some potential benefits. Contrary to what most people believe, such shift could lead to a step in the right direction in building a cleaner world. Implementing a wider usage of solar and wind generators could result in the reduction in CO2 output, which harms environment and creates many types of pollution. Thus, in turn, the shift such energy source can curb environmental issues like global warming and pollution. From an economic standpoint, the less dependence on fossil fuel can bring to free from the reliance on giant oil suppliers such as Russia and UAE. Embracing more renewable energy, countries can achieve political freedom and economic growth in the long run than the fossil fuel-based energy types. Therefore, I believe such turnover in the production of power could be preferable taking into several aspects such as economy and environment.

To conclude, I assert that promoting to utilize more renewable energy sources is generally a positive development despite above mentioned negatives.

question: Health problems such as obesity are often caused by changes in people's eating habits. What are the causes of this, and what solutions can be offered?
content:
There is a view that health related issues like obesity often derive from the shift in particular eating attitudes of people. while this trend can be linked to diverse reasons ranging from hectic lifestyle and food advertising, there are two several initiatives towards this common issue to deal with.

One major reason why people eat unhealthy is due to the busy lifestyle we run on a daily basis. When people have this ' on the go' lifestyle, they have a tendency to purchase things that are quick and straightforward to prepare, resulting in overall purchases of processed produce such as quick pasta and microwave requiring produce. Moreover, now while a family gathering is around the corner, and they have to go to cook hub and make something, people opt to drive to a restaurant or a fast food outlet. All these convenient foods embrace sodium, fat and sugar that are detrimental to health, leading to diseases in the long run if consumed too much and obesity issues. Furthermore, food advertising is another trigger of the situation. Shelves of supermarkets appears segregated. They are mostly designed for popular foods - for example the ones people see on the television adverts such as children's cereals, microwave ' vegetable' rice or the latest flavor of popular alcohol. The result of which is the placement of healthy food in less appealing shelves of supermarkets, where the attention of consumers is less likely to be drawn. Also, this advertising usually focuses on packaged food being affordable and instant to prepare; as a result, fresh food seems rather expensive and difficult to prepare.

All these above mentioned drivers of unhealthy eating behaviors of people can be eliminated via several measurements. First of all, there should be legislated laws against the advertisement of unhealthy produce on media. This could be done through promoting companies to produce healthier products and remove all additives and preservatives from products, and make them follow health-oriented manufacturing practices. Furthermore, second initiative towards healthy consumption is associated with fostering a sense of consciousness about the importance of healthy eating. Social media and tv can be used to create awareness about unhealthy produce, or holding social events against processed food could do the trick. This could make everyone familiar with what is healthy to eat, and pursue more organic food. Additionally, the reduction in the price of organic food is also a desirable act against unhealthy food. As above mentioned, healthy foods now cost expensive. If reduced in price, these types of food could be available to all layers of community.

In conclusion, it is evident that food adverts and busy lifestyle of people are the primary reasons to make eating habits worse, and cultivating social awareness, price reduction of organic food, setting up limits on packaged food can be steps to a healthier world.

question: Some people think that spending money on space exploration is a waste of resources, and that the money should be used to improve the quality of life on Earth. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
For the last century, there has been a number of projects on space exploration, and it is commonly argued that it is completely inefficient use of resources when money instead ought to be allocated for the improvement of life quality. However, I believe that such space expeditions have their own benefits, and should not be put off.

Admittedly, having a range of existing problems on the earth, it seems unjustifiable to invest on space exploration. There are countries having economic issues, and environmental problems such as global warming and diverse pollution types. Having said that, Space exploration can benefit in different ways. question: The cost of public transport is rising in many countries. What are the reasons for this, and what can be done about it?
content:
Increased production costs and other many reasons are contributing to the surge in prices around the world in services, and there is a view that The continuous rise in the cost of public transportation is being observed now. While there are some reasons that can explain why this is the case, a number of measures can be taken to mitigate the problem.

the causes of a rise in public transport fees are varied. One major explanation can be rising fuel prices for road transport. Having some global crisis like wars in the European union and the echoes of the pandemic, all these have resulted in such a trend in the fee of public transport, and some countries are probably run out of their power supply. As a result, these countries have no choice but purchasing fuel from other countries, the expenses of which add extra weight to the price of transportation. One more potential cause can be linked to environmental regulations. As renewable energy is being encouraged in many countries, governments worldwide are imposing stricter environmental standards to combat the use of fossil fuels. This initiative ,in turn, results in oftentimes in a rise of operational costs while they are environmentally beneficial.

One of the practical ways to reduce fees of public transport is government subsidies. Allocating funds to subsidize public transport services, there can be a decline in the operational costs for transport providers, allowing them to lower ticket prices. For instance, countries like Germany and France offer subsidized tickets to encourage public transport usage, therein increasing environmental friendly projects. Another solution can be legislating ridership programs, where regular users of public transport such as student s and employees can be issued with annual or monthly discounts on transport. This sort of measurement can offer free or heavily discounted rides during off-peak hours.

In conclusion, Although an increase in fees of transport can be linked to rising fuel costs and eco-friendly laws, these can be curbed via user-centralized measures.

question: Some people believe that the main reason people work is to earn money. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

Whereas, I firmly assert that this idea is flawed, and reasons like personal fulfillment and development bear more weight.

Moreover, for some it may be to achieve their long-wanted dreams like purchasing dreams houses or cars, and of course money is something that no one can reject and many crave for.

However, there is a diverse number of factors for working determined for a long time. A key factor contributing to this is the personal growth. While working for a company during the long period, individuals can gain self-benefits: boosting their skills, gaining experience and learning teamwork skills. Moreover, facing difficulties in the workplace can sharpen personal character of a person, and continuous communication and travels within the work can assist these workers to expand their connections, familiarizing with people from different backgrounds, which , in turn, can be practical when building their own business down the track. Have taken into consideration these advantages, people may be driven to exertion in work.

Another intrinsic motivation at work people seek is oftentimes enjoyment. People find it more beneficial to work in a healthy working environment, and enjoy the process everyday although their pay may be lower compared to other professions or the same positions in other companies. This is often contributed by the need for a supportive work setting and colleagues, as they can be deemed to continue working for this company in a long term. As seen oftentimes in Japan, due to long work hours most of the people are socially effected in a way that most of them end up drop-outs from work, or tend to spend their time in entertaining places to unwind form harsh work setting despite a higher salary and standards of living in this country.
