question: Some people think that new technology will help to reduce crime. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
The technology has brought many shifts into the way how we live and perceive things, and some tend to think that these technological breakthroughs can help to mitigate crime-related issues. I , however, believe that this idea is not completely flawless as crime is not directly linked to the technology.

Technological spinoffs in diverse fields can serve as a deterrent for potential crimes. Since the development in surveillance technology, crime rate has declined significantly. Being aware of monitoring through them, criminals are less likely to commit a crime, and face recognition and scanning cameras have also contributed to this trend greatly.

Having said that, social media and the internet has given a rise to new types of crime in the society. There is now the greatest crime ratio in the world than ever before due to mainly violation on the internet. one example of such situation can be online harassment, where the anonymity of users on the internet has made it possible to engage in online abuse, stalking and harassment. Unfortunately, there are not solutions to this problem as far as cybersecurity ends the operation of the website to curb this crime.

Furthermore, it is foolish to assume that technology can be linked to crime rate as in some low-tech environments, crime continues to thrive as it has always, without any direct impact of modern advancements. This is true especially when traditional crimes, such as theft, assault and murder, still occur without the use of technology. Rather relying on the idea that technology can do the trick to reduce criminal attitude, it is better to rise social awareness about the outcomes of crime, and implement stricter regulation on those who commit a crime.

In conclusion, Technology does not assist completely in the reduction of crime, whereas it surges this trend by providing a convenient space for new types of crime, and the reliance on such idea is unjustifiable.

question: Some people believe that success depends mainly on personal qualities such as hard work and determination, while others think that factors like money and appearance are more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: Some people think that watching videos is a more effective way to learn about other cultures than traditional methods such as reading books. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

question: Some people say that advertising has less influence on consumers today than it did in the past. Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative development?
content:
Advertising has been of importance to encourage consumers to buy more for many years, yet there is a view that not people of these days are effected by advertising campaigns compared to the past. While there are several justifiable factors driving this shift, I firmly assert that this is far a positive trend than the negative.

Reasons behind why the effect of advertising is fading away can be linked to add fatigue. With such a high volume of ads, where all the tv commercials, social media pop-up adds, and digital platforms, people are exposed to adds more than ever before to such an extent that they subconsciously ignore advertising massages. This constant exposure, in fact, leads to desensitization, making ads less impactful. Moreover, another potential explanation can be the advent in technology and consumer tools. Being less manipulated and with less overwhelming ad massages, people may feel less pressure to buy things they do not need, which can result in more autonomous decisions, and better management of their budgets. Furthermore, Increased media literacy and de-influencing trend can cause what is known as reclaim of the control over their choices. Taking into account these factors, less exposure to advertising campaigns can yield favorable outcomes.

In conclusion, the reduced responsiveness to advertising massages can be triggered by add fatigue and tools helping to refrain from ads, yet is capable of producing positive results thereof.

question: In many cities, more and more people live in small apartments without any outdoor space. What are the causes of this, and is it a positive or negative development?

question: Some people think that watching films and TV programmes about history is the best way to learn about the past. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

question: Some people think that looking after elderly people should be the responsibility of the government, while others believe it is the responsibility of their families. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
there is a view that taking care of the elderly should be a responsibility of the government. However, there are those who assume that this is the consideration of these people taking into account several reasons. Personally, I support the latter view in two main factors.

On the one side, there is a moral obligation of each country over their subjects, meaning that they should give support as much as possible for those who served for their country. As people age, elderly people may not become self-sufficient, being less able in terms of financial matters or physical even. Therefore, the government should meet the daily needs of these people such as pension, healthcare and housing. Moreover, when the government shows compassion and responsibility for their elderly, it creates a sense of unity and cohesion among citizens, making them have a respect and gratitude towards their country. Meantime, the government can also, thus, reduce a risk of creating poverty, homelessness and healthcare complication among its citizens, leading to better well-being and a more dignified life in their later years thereby.

I , however, support those who think that people should save for their old age. Firstly, it can encourage personal responsibility. Being self-sufficient is useful in a way that it might avoid extra burden on taxpayers while people can plan for their retirement and not rely on the government for financial support. After which, they can live their elderly years financially independent.

Furthermore, another potential reason to urge personal savings is sustainable economy; in other words, relying on personal savings rather than government support helps to create a more sustainable economy. If the government always provides financial aid to the elderly, it could place a heavy burden on the national budget, resulting in higher taxes or even public debt.

In conclusion, while moral duty is the reason to support elderly for the government, I assert that personal savings are important, taking into account reasons such as personal responsibility and economic stability.

question: Some people think that a well-functioning modern city needs an efficient public transport system above all, while others think other requirements are more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: Some people think that taxes should be increased to pay for better public services such as education and transport. Others believe this puts too much financial pressure on citizens. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
it is widely argued that there should be higher taxes received to enhance public facilities, including education and transport systems;however, the opponents of this view assert that the trend is not justifiable considering the huge financial burden on citizens. Personally, I believe that while having increased taxes for national improvement, the downsides of this should not also be neglected.

On the one side, higher taxes on people can mean several challenges to the community, especially the extra financial constraint. This can be true when most of the society lives under average wealth ratio, as this shift can strongly shorten the amount of money people can allocate to basic living needs. Moreover, Extended families can also significantly take disadvantage from this sort of change, since it may become more difficult for breadwinners of the family to support the family, meantime, most of the income goes to taxes.

From my perspective, implementing fixed taxes that may not put pressure on the living of common people is essential. To conclude, while for some increased taxation can bring benefits, there are also counterarguments to this shift. However, fair taxation that looks up to the income of citizens and focus on improving the life quality is a favorable resolution.

question: Many old buildings in cities reflect the traditions and lifestyles of earlier generations. Some people think these old buildings should be preserved. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

While there are certain kinds of them to be protected, I assume that upsides of such architecture, such as reflecting the cultural heritage and attracting tourists, are far favorable than downsides.

Cultural and religious buildings are the types that should be under protection due to the significance they place. This is because that the cultural buildings, including opera houses, museums and theaters, play an intrinsic role in preserving the cultural and national identity of the country. They are great tools to determine what is forgotten and remembered over centuries. Moreover, There is also a huge importance of religious buildings to locals which makes preservation of them more reasonable. One major reason is it to do with the values, faith and beliefs people have on these spaces. These are considered sacred and central to worship, prayer and religious rituals.

I, however, believe that considering above mentioned factors preserving such architecture can greatly benefit to the country. One of the most significant benefits is the cultural education. Cultural buildings are the living evidence of the situations happened in the past that has developed over the time. These buildings, in turn, can help people especially the young to learn about history in an interesting way, and visiting a historical site is often more memorable and engrossing than reading a textbook. In addition, having a range of historical sites can mean increased number of tourists. Historical places oftentimes may allure many tourists all over the world, and this helps local business and workshops to grow economically as they rise their sales. It can also create many workplaces, helping native people find a way to make a living.

In conclusion, while the most valuable types of historical buildings are cultural and religious ones, I feel that they can do the trick boosting the economy of the country and preserving the local culture or educating younger generation, thus surpassing the drawbacks.

question: Some people think that environmental education should be taught at school, while others believe it is the parents' responsibility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: Some people think that newspapers are the best way to learn about the news, while others believe the internet is better. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

question: In many countries, tourists visit museums more often than local people do. Why is this the case? What can be done to encourage local people to visit museums?
content:
Museums have a great role providing practical information about the country's customs and traditions, and it is oftentimes argued that these cultural institutions are a commonplace among tourists, whereas the native people take a little interest in visiting them. While the driving factors for the popularity of museums is their educational roles, there are a number of ways to make them appeal to locality, such as organizing special events and establishing discount on the entries.

One of the main reasons why museums are go-to destinations for tourists is the chance for broader information about the local culture. when visiting a particular place, the one thing tourists might crave for is the greater data, such as about background of the place, local traditions, architecture and to name just a few, and these tourists choose the museums as they can fulfill these requirements to the fullest. These cultural and educational institutions can provide all the intrinsic information they might need to know. Not only do museums provide such possibility of information, but can also they facilitate special programs. For example, nowadays there are visualized tours next to exhibitions held in most of the museums around the world, giving one in a lifetime experience to tourists. Plus, they can also organize tours around the city to show some of the remaining historical sites and offer details about historic landmarks.

The engagement among the local people towards museums can be urged in a number of ways. One such approach can be the organization of events in the museum. They can hold interactive and fun games or structured events like music events, lectures or themed activities in the museums to gain fame among those living in the local area. Notably, by providing children with indoor specialized activities, they can also increase the number of the attendees. These events hosted in museums can provide unique experiences that encourage repeat visits in the long run.

Furthermore, another potential way of rising popularity of museums can be the discounts on tickets to them. Implementing special discounts or free-entry days for local residents can be an efficient way of rising an interest. Moreover, Museums can offer exclusive membership programs for those who live nearby, and these programs can include perks like free admission, discount at the museum store or early access to new exhibits. These types of membership can create a sense of belonging among local people, and increasing frequent visits thereby. While Museums make most of their revenue from tourists, they can attract more people.

In conclusion, it is undeniable that the most apparent reason to pay a visit to museums for tourists is to be informed. While these institutions are not well-popularized among local inhabitants, structured events and special entry offers can do the trick, therefore increasing the volume of local attendees.

question: Some people think that one of the best ways to solve environmental problems is to increase the cost of fuel for cars and other vehicles. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
Taking a right approach towards mitigating environmental issues comprise different measurements, among which increased price of fuels for transportation is oftentimes considered as the most effective one. While I acknowledge that it brings about several advantages, I mostly disagree with this view in two factors.

Admittedly, there are a number of benefits to rising the fuel price up. One of which is surely the reduction in air pollution. As far as the damage towards environment is considered, the most ubiquitous pollution is the emitted air, which is in most cases the carbon dioxide produced by cars. Once the number of cars is declined on roads because of the increased fuel prices, the air can become cleaner as it did , for instance, back in the period of COVID 19 pandemic. During a certain period, the volume of traffic was reduced greatly, resulting in the less release of carbon dioxide. Therefore, high cost of fuel can ensure the way to deal with the environmental problems.

However, this would not solve the problem alone, since there are other polluters that impact on the nature negatively. Increasing the fuel cost, on the other hand, can lead to several major problems in the society. One apparent example is the economic slowdown and inflation. Rising fuel prices may increase the production and transportation costs in a way that it leads to higher prices for goods and services; as a result of which, there can be a financial strain on both businesses and citizens. This increased inflation can mean the less power of purchasing among people that eventually can slow down the economic growth of the country.

Furthermore, the increase in the poverty level in a society is another area that is effected by high oil prices. Due to their nature of limited recourses, higher prices of fuel can bear a greater financial burden to low income families, where the most of the income is directed to purchase basic necessities like daily household items or food, and this sort of shift in their life can mean even greater pressure in their life. This also can push borderline households below poverty line that comes with result of weak socio economic condition of the society.

In conclusion, although high oil prices can aid to cope with the environmental issues, I completely believe that it is far negative, especially in terms of economic aspects.

question: Some people think that team sports are the best way to teach children to cooperate at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Having said that, I assert that not every children are able to play outdoor sports due to the fact that they may have a type of disability or can be shy to work together with others. In conclusion, while it is admitted that team sports can teach certain important skills, taking into account the benefits of other approaches to teach collaboration, I completely feel that these approaches far outweigh the former way of teaching children cooperation.

question: Some people think that governments should make public transport free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

While it can be a heavy financial constraint on the government, I completely believe that it comes with several advantages for both dwellers and the society.

Funding all costs of providing free access to transport can be difficult for the government, where it also should supply salaries to those who service in this sector too. Without money collected by commuters, it can impact negatively on the economy of the country, when this funding can be directed to other purposes such as pollution and healthcare. Therefore, some can propose that it is not justifiable to make public transit free of charge.

I, however, would argue that there are counter arguments, and free-fare transit can benefit in different ways. First of all, there are environmental benefits. Fewer cars on the road can mean fewer CO2 is emitted, which results in a cleaner air in urban areas, as well as due to a heavy traffic cities may face noise pollution problems, and this can also find its solution by this legislation. In the long term, this legislation can have positive impact on people's well being and inner city environment.

Furthermore, this regulation can significantly reduce traffic and congestion. Having free-access public transit, it is more likely that commuter numbers increase, leading fewer private vehicles on the road. This , in turn, can result in the lesser number of traffic congestion. Moreover, government-funded free public transport can deal with problems like space shortage, as public transport do not require space as much as private ones do, and parking issues can be also solved, resulting in the better city scape without any heavy traffic of cars.

In conclusion, government-funded free public transport can benefit to the area's environment and lessen traffic issues. Therefore, I strongly feel that it is a must-prioritize legislation in every country.

Online tracking has also become a part of our daily digital live, powered by website trackers, cookies, and other technologies. This collected information can be used against users in ways such that personalized advertisement can be created by AI to influence consumers' decisions to unnecassary purchases, leading to manipulation and deceptive marketing practises. Moreover, tracking data can be sold to data brokers or shared with third parties, who can utilize it to engage in social engineering tacts and crafting convincing scams, exposing individuals to potential harm. It is thus vital that companies ensure safe ways to track personal information or ask a user's permission to engage in any actions.

In conclusion, there are greater number of risks when companies use online clouds to store personal information of individuals compared to advantages, such as offering unlimited storage space.

question: Countries are becoming more and more similar to each other, sharing the same fashion, culture, food and lifestyles. Is this a positive or negative development?
content:
There is a new rising trend - homogenization - a phenomenon in which countries tend to share common treats, losing unique aspects of their own, such as fashion, culture, daily activities and eating habits. Despite this shift is , to some extent, favorable in terms of travelling opportunities, I support each nation keeping its uniqueness.

Homogenization can be reckoned as a desirable shift, as it opens doors of opportunities.The most apparent one is increased chances of convenient travels across the globe. With the most of the countries having similar habits, like eating or speaking a familiar language, there can be far fewer challenges for tourists while touring in another country, avoiding obstacles , for instance, language barrier, diet and cultural differences. Additionally, students may be benefiters of this trend, What international tourists confront oftentimes while doing their courses abroad is mostly the hardship that comes with living abroad, an ability to communicate and culture-shock could be eliminated.

From my perspective, this does not mean it is completely advantageous as there are risks to having similirities across nations. The loss of the unique traditions and customs of cultures is the main issue. While there are hundreds of nations with mesmorizing and unrepeatable traditions, which , in fact, have evolved in thousand years, the above mentioned shift could result in the disappearance of these cultures, or at least it could reduce the number of potential travel destinations. Traditional clothing fabrics and garments, and foods are evident examples of what might be lost in the long run.

Another reason is clearly to do with the pressure to come from major and developed countries over their counterparts. It is frequently true that impoverished countries are the ones that take the damage while rich ones impact their clothing, diet and daily choice decisions as people want to imitate people from those wealthy nations in the pursuit of acquiring the same progress of development. Consequently, this absurd game of imitation leads to the loss identity. Moreover, with the introduction of international companies local business can be under the threat and competition to which, they can struggle to compete with. Thus, it is vital to have identity and habits unlike each other for countries.

In conclusion, despite advantages homogenization has to offer, it could not be still favorable shift,while I believe its drawbacks make it greatly less desirable, leading to the identity loss and manipulation of huge countries.

question: In some countries, school summer holidays last two or three months. Some people think these holidays should be shorter. Do the advantages of shorter holidays outweigh the disadvantages?
content:
Summer holidays, lasting about two or three months are a commonplace among some countries, and it is true that such holidays mostly come in the favour of school teachers, concerning about their mental and physical well being. However, shortened holidays could potentially have a toll on their parents and reduce their academic performance.

Summer school holidays mostly benefit employers of education sector, as after 9 or 8 months continuous work pressure, teachers and staff of the school can have a chance to enjoy their time. It is true that these professions are far demanding compared to other workplaces, since difficulty of teaching students and managing their behaviour is greater than any profession. Plus, constant work and teaching could potentially have mental toll on teachers; summer holidays offer teachers an opportunity to recharge, and they also can spend quality time with their family, building a stronger rapport with them.

Furthermore, children are able to relax after constant schoolwork, early mornings and exams, as a result of which these can have on children mental and physical tolls. Summer vacation offers them a much-needed break. Being free from the pressures of school, it allows their minds and bodies to rest. Summer vacation is vital so that they return to class refreshed, motivated, and full of energy.

Summer vacations, being a chance for relaxation for students and teachers, have negative sides too, which is why some opt for shorter vacations. One of the most significant factors to this is the concern on the decline of academic performance of children. Long breaks can reduce thier skills and knowledge, which they acquire during almost the whole year, for children usually avoid learning while they are on holidays, and they focus on more having fun.

Another argument in favour of shortened summer vacation is the impact of it on the social-emotional well-being of students. This is mostly apparent in the case of adolescents, who are more likely to suffer easily from social and emotional issues. Social isolation is observed oftentimes in young adults, when their social circles and routines are disrupted, to which they are accustomed to during the school year. They feel lonely and isolated from their classmates and friends.

I also believe that parents can have challenges during summer vacations that usually tend to last 2 or 3 monts. Having a responsibility to take care of children and balance their work and family life during summer can result in increased stress and obstacles. These can lead to mental and physical burnout, while school, apart from being a place for education for children, could provide extra curriculum activities for children, and making it easier for parents to have some time for themselves and relax after work. It is , thus, important to have shorter summer vacation/

In conclusion, school vacations are much important to avoid academic burnout of children and allow teachers to take some relaxation time, while these holidays display some downsides, which call for the introduction of shortened vacations.

question: Some people believe that young people's reading and writing skills are getting worse because they use electronic devices to communicate. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
Undeniably the use of technologies especially gadgets has an integral role in people's life, and there is a view that as young people continue to utilize these devices to communicate, their literacy skills like writing and reading abilities can take a toll. I , however, would assert that this idea is completely flawed unless AI based systems are avoided, although it displays strong counterarguments.

Arguments towards the decline in academic performances of students, who are using modern devices to keep in touch, may seem valid. One significant factor contributing can be less dependency on natural approaches towards writing and reading. Since technologies are developed to the point where AI featured software is able to impact on our writing and reading skills, they provide autonomous spell and grammar check features, which come useful in situations where a user makes a mistake. With this on their minds, most of the students write carelessly. In terms of reading, now the same exact software also confer AI chats, which can identify and provide the key points from long texts in an instant, which otherwise would require an hour or so from students. Hence, some can argue that these factors are drivers of the illiterate generation.

Having said that, from my presumption these gadgets do not influence negatively on children's literacy skills in general. It is because of the digital literacy. With opportunities like social media and news platform, children are more exposed to reading on these platforms, where they engage in reading blogs, news, subtitles and online books ever more, for example. These activities can potentially enhance their passive and active reading habits, thus improving their reading fluency.

Furthermore, writing skills can be reinforced through daily communication, which young people make during conversation on chats and social media apps. This frequent writing can boost, even in informal settings, their writing clarity, coherence, and expression. To illustrate, there are a number of social media platforms to exchange ideas for teenagers, including Reddit, Discord and X - formerly known as Twitter.

I , however, feel that these perspectives are flawless when users do not show any dependency on AI generated features on their gadgets, either on mobile phones or computers. Constant exposure to these features can reduce their writing and reading clarity in the long term, effecting children's critical thinking, creativity and active reading habits. Therefore, it is of importance that a person avoid tendency towards these software systems or have a limit of usage.

In conclusion, digital devices have no negative effects on children's literacy skills as they encourage exposure to language through digital media, as far as I believe, avoiding AI and auto features is preferable though.

question: More and more people are buying labour-saving devices such as microwaves and rice cookers for their homes. Is this a positive or negative development?
content:
The consumerism ratio has increased radically in the last few years, and with this the tendency to purchase labour-saving devices for households like television, microwave ovens and rice cookers had become a commonplace. While this trend can pose several negatives, mainly concerning the well-being of consumers, I reckon that these devices can assist people in several ways, such as increased quality of life and economic boost.

Admittedly, household appliances can come with the health risks. For example, it oftentimes result in the reduced physical activity. As households become more advanced and equipped with technologies, people start doing less activities, and most of the time they end up spending excessive time online and indoors. This situation can cause health risks: obesity may appear as a problem and such related illnesses because of the reduced movement.

Nevertheless, as far as I believe these modern devices actually come in favour of users. Firstly, they can be time-saving in a way that people would allocate the time, previously spent on chores, to hobbies or learning new skills, having a chance for personal growth, and it can also be convenient, especially for elderly and disabled people, those who struggle to do tasks like cleaning and washing, as they have weaker bodies and less strength.

Another significant positive aspect of using devices at home is that it can encourage consumerism. Due to an increase in demand for such products, this boosts manufacturing, retail and technological innovations. Therefore, it can run the economy of the country and the income of people in a large scale, increasing the volume of import and export of the country.

In conclusion, although increased consumerism of household gadgets may seem unfavorable as it impacts the health of people, I still find it more appealing, mainly dur to reasons like economic breakthrough and modern conveniences.

question: Some people think that governments should provide housing for people who cannot afford to buy their own. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

Of course, there are factors explaining this view, but I assert that introducing government-funded housing at no charge is the most plausible idea in two key reasons.

Among other basic necessities, housing stands the most significant for dignity and survival, and given the fact that citizens contribute to government revenue through taxation, it is government's responsibility to offer equitable access to housing at no cost.

I, however, believe that it does not work this way in most cases,since not everyone is a taxpayer, while taxes are mostly channeled to provide safety and pension systems, not housing. There are actually several downsides of such programs. Firstly, it can increase dependency of citizens on the country negatively. Instead of working in different industry sectors or companies, people may initiate rely on government funding, which results in the reduction of work ethics and productivity. Being the most high-cost necessity people purchase in their life, housing usually drives people to earn money and helps the country to maintain workplaces and economy.

Another negative side might be linked to financial strain on government fund. While there are already several vital areas to invest, such as health, education, road infrastructure and to name just a few, housing can be additional burden on the fund, and may strain the economy. As a result, free housing projects can lead to national debt.

In conclusion, although it is true that government has responsibility in front of the public to confer need of citizens, this idea is not always flawless, as there are other areas that country should focus on, and also free housing can make people dependent on such programs, resulting in several economic risks.

content:

question: Some people believe that new technologies have helped to reduce crime. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

question: Some people think that economic growth is the best way to measure a country's success, while others believe other types of progress are equally important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
A country can be classified as a successful one by various means of progress, and there is a view that economic increase is one apparent factor among these, while there are those who feel that it is not the only, as other developments can confer countries with prosperity. I, however, would argue that the former view is far favorable, although geographical location and education systems may come equal in this regard.

While I am of the opinion that economic progress is a key to an affluent country, I also acknowledge the fact that the location where a country is based in and the quality of education play an intrinsic role therein. Firstly, a location of the country can matter in several terms, where a rich location can confer access a country to natural resources like gold, metal, coal and gas - the resources that oftentimes make a country wealthy. Moreover, high quality of education may bring many high-promising and talented youth that will serve for the good of the country in the long term, while they contribute to scientific developments in this country.

Said that, in my presumption, of course, the key to success lies on the economic growth due to several reasons. One argument in favor of this is the higher living standards that come with it. When economies expand, this surely brings income rise, leading to better housing, education and healthcare. One valid example can be transformation of south Korea, which witnessed rapid economic boost in 1990s; as a result, the nation flourished and living of common people became more prosperous.

In conclusion, without any doubt the economic growth is by far the most important factor to a successful country, as far as i am concerned. However, it should not be neglected that geographical position and education quality are also of importance.

question: Some people think that governments should control the amount of fresh water people use, while others believe individuals should be free to use as much as they want. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:

Personally, I support the former view in reasons - the prevention of future shortages, and water is not unlimited source.

On the one hand, it is reasonable to point that people do as they wish with water, as it is their basic human right. Water, along with other natural resources that are abundant and free, is non-government estate, which should not be in consideration to put a limit on consumption. To prevent a scenario where there will be conflicts over this resource, which is for now ubiquitous, the responsible entities should execute water conversation measures. As far as I know, one European country has already taken such a step, in which it uses recycling projects to filter waste water, and also there are practices like re-using water from rains and drainages, which can be solutions to long-terms sustainability.

Furthermore, many may think water is finite resource, and it can be used for thousands of years. Like any other natural resource water is someday going to run-off, leading to detrimental outcomes. With having children informed about its importance in education institutions, there ought to be also public awareness campaigns - actions that can aid and fend the idea off - 'water is not limited'.

In conclusion, our idea about infinite water resource is fully flawed, and there government should impose regulations and awareness about the vitality of water, as future shortages may arise.

question: Interest in space tourism has grown in recent years. Some people think it should be encouraged. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:

Currently, a handful of private companies are offering an opportunity for individuals, known as space tourists, and these companies usually, but not always, target a sizeable revenue from it, like SpaceX by Elon musk or Jeff Bezos. As promoters of this trend, in fact, suggest that it can be a stunning chance of experiencing non-gravitational state of space and relish the intrinsic beauty of space, where those who might have dreamt of going to space, can manage to achieve their dreams, for instance.

It is, nevertheless, not a perfect promising industry of tourism. First of all, going to and back space requires a huge amount of resources and expense, and come at the cost of ecology as it requires going through the atmosphere layer - The ozone layer - which is fragile and the most vital part of ecosystem. This barrier usually avoids harmful sun rays from entering our atmosphere, and travelling through it means destroying a part of it that might have a detrimental and lasting influence of the environment, triggering climate change even.

It also further can be supported by the fact - this could be the pleasure of high status and wealthy people, where such travel tickets can cost at enormous prices -anywhere from hundreds of thousands to tens of millions of dollars -,and this is mainly because there is financial propulsion by aforementioned companies. These enterprises cater solely to exceptionally wealthy people. Ironically, this can lead to a sense of public disillusionment with space: Instead of opening it up to everyone, it might cause people to roll their eyes at the inaccessibility. Basically, it's just rich people doing rich-people things.

In conclusion, I believe that there is more harm than good in the industry, so called space tourism. question: Some people believe that watching TV and playing computer games is harmful to children's development. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
Indisputably, screen time among children has increased at unprecedented rate, and it is believed that as they continue to watch tv and play computer games, these are not going to help their cognitive performance, yet I tend to think otherwise. Apart from being negative to health and social life of children, controlled screen time can boost digital fluency and yield some benefits.

Of course,the more children spend on screen alone at home, the more they are susceptible to zone out from the outside world. Now, it is a casual occurrence for a child to sit in front of tv or their video game sets for hours instead of having the joy of outside laughter and face-to-face interactions. Although a child can have thousands of online friends, they profoundly feel lonely in real life. This is because the excessive screen time can lead to the decline in communication skills, and real friends are made not online, but in real life conversations.

Moreover, digital overexposure can result in detrimental health risks. Oftentimes, inactive lifestyle spent in front of tv for hours children can develop negative health effects. For example, not being able to burn daily calories and do exercises or movement to make blood run all throughout the body, people develop back-pain in their early days or poor posture. Such a lifestyle has also been proven to trigger obesity in many cases. Therefore, children can develop health risks at a young age, and what happens after 20 or 30 years is the worst scenario.

Being said that, I still assert that it is possible to gain benefits from watching tv or playing video games. The first benefit has to do with cognitive skill enhancement. When children are exposed to games and tv programs that challenge their thinking, several brain areas can be reinforced,say, when playing strategy games requiring resource management and planning, and their critical thinking and reasoning can be reinforced. Games - popular and relate to this regard - are Minecraft, puzzles, and world-building games in which creativity is used at its best.

Another hefty upside of spending time on screen can be a chance to build up educational knowledge and skill acquisition. Sometimes, wondering how to play video games or watching tv, children may unconsciously initiate learning basic coding or software operation. Plus, there are dozens of tv channels(National geographics, Pyramid, Around the world, BBC and to name a few) that air useful programs like language learning or documentaries about nature through which children can be brought to be informed about outside world. At times, these can spark a curiosity to these fields and guide children to their future career paths. Minecraft, for instance, is not only about world building, but also requires fundamental codes in modes like ' code builder', where a simple task like building a door that opens automatically introduces a child to a basic' if -then' statement in coding.

In conclusion, despite what excessive time can impact on children's brain and connection with others, I am convinced that there are far greater advantages of it such as skill and education related ones that can be of use down the track.

question: Despite many efforts to reduce pollution, the problem continues to get worse. Why is this the case, and what can be done to solve it?
content:
There are a huge number of attempts being committed to mitigate pollution and alike issues, yet tangible results cannot be seen. While economic fear is the most important reason to this phenomenon along with urban expansion, measures to solve them can be enforcing stronger regulations and investment in green technology.

One of the foremost reasons lies in the economic factor. This is in most of the countries dominant over ecological well-being, where these countries are afraid to impose regulations and limitations on behemoth industries, as it might lead to several detrimental causes: job losses, reduced revenue, economic crisis, the rise of poverty, and to name a few. Factories, for instance, in developing countries like India and China continue to emit greenhouse gases despite international commitments to reduce them, for they are the main sources of tax revenue even though there are green laws in existence.

Urban expansion can be blamed down in this regard. The more people move to cities, at more rapid level the pollution surges. This can be explained by the fact that overpopulation and ever increasing vast number of people exacerbate pollution at every level — from overcrowded cities filled with vehicles to the uncontrolled spread of waste in residential areas, meaning that it becomes more challenging for the government to control pollution levels because there is now more demand for energy, water, and waste disposal.

Of course, there are silver bullets to tackle these problems. One such effective initiative is to implement stronger green laws to a point, where it becomes a common sense and obligatory for people to follow rules. The government can tax fines on those who break regulations: not fixed ones but depending on the salary ratio of the offender so as to ensure that even wealthy residents cannot escape from rules. Such a strict system of environment protection can be seen in European countries like Sweden and Norway, where a person has to answer for their actions on the environment regardless of societal status.

Plus, directing efforts towards countering non-renewable energy such as coal or oil and promoting renewable energy can do the trick. Although the amount of opposition against ecological damage, there are still thousands or tens of thousands of factories dependent on conventional fuels — the main drivers of air and water pollution around the world. While countries transition to sources — such as solar, wind, and hydro power, emissions can be cut drastically. Moreover, encouraging innovation in clean energy, electric cars, and waste recycling can create jobs while this also helps to protect the environment. Examples under this point are aforementioned ones, where there are tax incentives for electric cars, raising awareness about the importance of using clean energy.

In conclusion, the problem of not going far in terms of environmental protection can be concerns on economy of the country as well as increased population in cities, whilst deterrents are stricter green laws and the exhortation of renewable energy.

question: Loneliness and poor health are common problems among elderly people. What are the causes of these problems, and what can be done to solve them?
content:
it is scientifically believed that loneliness and reduced health conditions are main issues at old ages among people, and routinely exercising and staying in touch with other people have been introduced as deterrents to this trend. Of course, these detrimental conditions often occur as a result of passive social life of individuals, and aforementioned solutions are indeed effective, yet financial intensives can do the trick as well.

There are several causes of such emotional state among elderly people, among which one of the significant reasons is declined physical movement. As people age slowly, their daily routine starts to involve less actions — sitting in front of the tv and reading become a commonplace, where they spend less time outdoors socializing with people. In contrast, no many elderly devote their leisure time into passive activities and get isolated from outside, which results in feeling lonely and the well-being, in fact, is connected somehow into a person's emotional state. In Japan, for instance, there are people - known as hikikomori - who avoid social contact or stay confined to their rooms without any actual active lifestyle, and these include young men and older people mostly. Mental disorders such as anxiety, depression and stress are observed among these individuals. Therefore, inactive life style of seniors can be a key to their loneliness and poor health conditions.

Admittedly, encouraging them to engage in daily exercises is a great way to mitigate the issue. They, in turn, begin seeing hefty changes in their health and mental conditions, since it is proven that sporty lifestyle can shape one's mind and body simultaneously. Another solution can be making them involved more in real life conversations. As social being, humans need consistent communication and pleasing environment of other people, not only a way to share news and have conversations about daily happenings, but also a way to relieve their stress, and feel valued and alive.

These approaches are practical to some extent, but an alternative measure would be conferring financial incentives to these elderly. Oftentimes the reason behind reduced overall physical and mental health is a financial challenge they face. This is because many elderly people cannot afford the cost of health treatments or frequent visits to their family and friends. Providing financial support to them can offer greater autonomy and social participation: they can take part in community events, travel to family members, or engage in hobbies that keep them mentally stimulated and socially connected. Meantime, it helps also them to maintain a healthier lifestyle, ensuring that they can access adequate healthcare, live in proper housing conditions, and purchase nutritious food. For instance, government pensions in countries like Sweden and Japan have proven effective in improving life expectancy and reducing the incidence of depression among older adults.

In conclusion, while the main driver of loneliness and poor health is the reduced dynamic lifestyle, providing steady financial support can yield noticeable upsides greater than encouraging them to stay connected and doing sports more.

question: Some people believe that parents should decide how their children spend their free time, while others think children should be free to make their own choices. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
content:
The role parents play in their children's life is vital, and it is believed that they should be responsible bodies to manage their children's free time, where they can direct it for better. However, this is opposed by the view that it is children who should have freedom of choice in this regard, which I share my opinion with.

On the one hand, parental guidance in terms of free time management is an intrinsic element. First of all, it ensures that children spend their time productively and meaningfully.This is because parents are able to direct children’s time to educational and skill-building activities, which will help them in the long run. These activities can induce them to be responsible and disciplined, which results in less screen time on social media and video games. Parents plan and introduce them to sports or after-school clubs, so that their children are learning something instead of wasting their precious time, for instance.

Having said that, offering independence, as far as I am concerned, to children in controlling their leisure time can yield many benefits, where one hefty benefit is the encouragement of creativity and independence. Through this autonomy, children experiment with different interests and hobbies over time, and thus can find the thing they excel in and are motivated to pursue. Such attempts with trial and errors can lead to greater self-identity and choice, decision making skills and critical thinking along with motivation, say, children can take part in painting, outdoor activities and sports, and settle on one particular hobby, which they submerge themselves in. Such independence of choice is also opted by many parents around the world, since it teaches lifelong lessons and builds up confidence.

In summary, it is true that the role of parents in choice of past times plays a key role, guiding children to more efficient and practical activities, yet I reckon that individual preference of children is far beneficial, as it confers a chance for self - development.

question: Some people think that young people who commit crimes should be punished in the same way as adults. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
At present, rules about punishing people for their crime are being revised to produce the fairest verdict, and it is believed that a universal punishment should be given to the youth as it is done to adults. I do admit why this idea is being put forward, yet such a change in the court would do more harm than good.

It is undisputable that everyone who is showing criminal behaviour does it consciously, even young people. Plus, given fixed punishment in the society, the government can achieve less crime ratio compared to the current situation. This is mainly because if treated equally, people can be aware of outcomes of their actions and be less likely to commit crimes, where it can lead to reduced crime scenes in the community, and it does more imply to young generation who may consider their behaviour with increased consideration knowing they would end up in the same scenario as seniors do; for instance, if a young person commits a serious offence, lenient treatment can display reverse effects and encourage more crimes among such ages. Plus, harsh penalties may deter other young people from engaging in similar illegal activities.

However, as far as I am concerned that young people should receive completely different treatment for their offence for these key reasons. Firstly, it is scientifically proven that the human brain continues to develop until mid twenties, meaning that there can be chances to change individuals behaviour. If given less severe punishment and rehabilitation programs to young offenders, while it can serve as a deterrent for future offences. Such initiative are put in use, for example, in European countries, where young offenders, regardless of their crime, oftentimes serve a particular amount of days in a correctional colonies.

Secondly, it is morally wrong to sent juveniles into prison with adults, as reasons for criminal behaviour for children can be different than adults'. Most of the children offenders, reportedly, are victims of sexual and domestic abuse, and some of them either are victims not realizing what they are doing. Sending these children to the jail with much elder criminals can yield more issues being emerged in their behaviour, which will influence probably to their future life. It is wrong to throw children to the same system we use for adult offenders and call it the justice. As aforementioned, the justice would be giving a second chance and help these children realize what is whether socially and morally wrong, thus guiding them into brighter future.

In conclusion, when it is true that most of the offence is done impulsively and similar charges can produce greater balance in the system, I remain convinced that a child's brain is not fully developed when they commit an offence; treating them differently with special programs and considering their circumstances thus are relatively effective options thereof.

question: In some countries, laws are being introduced to limit working hours. Some people think this is a positive development. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
Over the few decades, there has been tremendous number of positive changes on workplace aesthetics, and there is a common introduction of laws regarding limiting operating hours among countries, where the opinion of the employee should be considered by job givers. The main notion behind this is the increased opportunities for employees so as to balance their work and life, and this trend can be reckoned as a favorable shift as it is going to boost the productivity in the long run.

Maintaining the balance between work and life is one of the most struggling issues for most of the workers in different areas, which is why the limitation of work hours is put forward. After their graduation and being exposed to a new environment, most of the young employees find it extremely challenging to maintain a balance between work timetable and personal life hours. Some of them end up spending too much in their offices, oftentimes leading themselves to work burnout and too early loss of desire for the future, or might they be excessively relishing the joy of adulthood and spending most of their time on diverse leisure activities, whereas allocating time on career and self improvement becomes an inferior consideration. Hence, it is pretty reasonable to take their perceptions on business hours, and make their schedule flexible so that they might have an advantage and slowly fit in these profession relating responsibility while maintaining a well-balanced personal life borders.

This sort of change in work settings seems a flawless idea, One justification is that it literally helps to increase the productiveness in the long run. For example, having employees,who have no complaints about their work environments and are satisfied with their personal life, can mean that these workers are ready to be determined, hard-working, of course in this given short amounts of time in offices, and persistent in their designated tasks, resulting in more work-efficiency. This is mainly because they would have no worries about over-working or not being able to meet deadlines no more, which eases their worries about losing a job or devoting too much time to their families;for instance, such a legislation have been put into practice in several business offices in German companies, where workplace supervisors run a survey asking how much hours they should be working. After taking a collective response and implementing it, they witnessed several improvements in employee behaviors in their work places, no to mention an increased overall well being of them.

Furthermore, asking employees about their office hours is the prerequisite prevention towards employee retention and job-hopping among employees. It somehow creates a sense of belonging among employees, inducing them that they are valued in their current work settings and their management actually cares about them, which lessens the number of those leaving their jobs or considering to do so, a measurement we can call 'a long term retention strategy'. This strategy also gives an advantage over employee hiring, where they can sort out employees with suitable desires and traits to company's, and building up much stronger and coordinated teams, thus reducing frequent job changes.

In conclusion, while regulating office hours can be classifies as more of individual-benefit based helping young employees to achieve a better work and life balance, it is a promising transition, bringing about tangible benefits like increased productiveness and reduced employee retention and job changes.

question: Guided tours to remote areas of countries are becoming increasingly popular with tourists. Is this a positive or negative development?
content:
There is a growing number of planned guide tours to remote regions of countries, which are now pretty popular among tourists. This sort of travel packages usually damage the local environment, yet it is mostly positive as there are perks like economic upliftment and increased travel experience of individuals.

Undoubtedly, when there are far away places that experience overwhelming flow of tourists, there is always higher environmental footprint to be left. This is mainly due to the increased human activities in the region;for example, some tourists,unsurprisingly, are not environmentally consciousness, meaning that it is expected from them to throw away garbage or light fires in natural zones, leading to habitat disturbance and deterioration. Oftentimes, they leave diverse chemical or unprocessed food cans after them, which animals might consume and be contaminated, in the worst scenario the death of these creatures.

Having said that, such guided tours are able to yield far beneficial outcomes. Firstly, Constantly increasing number of tourists can drive the economy of the local community, as these tourists start an trade circle and bring foreign investment in local services or money, say, they purchase locally made traditional arts or use services like guides or translators: this also provides job opportunities to native people, where the quality of life can also be boosted. Plus, this foreign fundings can be used to invest in local touristic and entertaining projects to lure more travelers in the long run, say, some households in some countries confer homestays, so these families can earn money without any risks or prerequisite investment in businesses.

Plus, this travel opportunity can enrich personal experience of tourists.Places tourists visit are either major economic cities or diverse entertaining ones: Dubai, New York, Tokyo and such cities are good examples in the case, yet at present travelling overseas is less about experiencing the culture. During organized travels to villages and rural areas of the country, the exposure to authentic traditions and customs of the culture is likely to be higher than visiting aforementioned spots, resulting in increased awareness of local cultural heritage and thus witnessing once in a lifetime travel experience. Tour guides to Kyrgyzstan, for instance, are quite well-known in my country, where Uzbek people get a chance to submerge themselves in the culture and stunning nature of this neighboring nation.

In conclusion, a huge amount of continuous travelers might pose a threat to the local flora and fauna of the place, but these tours also mean an economic advantages to local people and foster authentic cultural exposure.

question: More and more people are moving to megacities with populations of 20 million or more. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
content:
Urbanization has been on the rise for the past few decades, and now it is believed that megacities that hold 20 million citizens or so are becoming more and more popular to move to. This trend is surely because of the advantage: urban places offer access to a wide range of opportunities, while I assert that moving to major cities is mostly unfavorable as it may lead to the environmental degradation and pressure on housing.

Of course, it is rational that why people strive to move to cities with bigger population is due to the chances they can obtain in different fields. Cities are homes for people of different backgrounds and skills, and thus it is easier for these people to share and exchange innovations and ideas. Moreover, there is also greater options regarding jobs and education; most megacities house large companies and universities, say, so-famous New York university is located on one of the largest city, New York. This might prove why even international students choose to study in major cities, as well as cities are hubs, offering variety of employment opportunities for individuals, while major companies like Coca Cola, Samsung, Apple are based in such cities.

With that being said, I remain convinced that the idea urbanization is positive is flawed. This is mainly because of the potential threat to the local environment of cities. More population moves to cities, more waste, pollution and transport mobility are created, all of which add strain on the environment. Take a single mass transit system in cities, as more people start to dwell in cities, more of them initiate utilizing public transport and private ones, and thus cars produce more carbon dioxide than ever before, a type of gas which is highly toxic to the atmosphere and one's well-being.

Furthermore, housing prices rise when cities become overcrowded, which is certainly a main issue for financially disabled people or low socio-economic families. To put it in simple words, aside having wider earning opportunities, cities are home to diverse individuals, ranging from really wealthy celebrities, businessmen, and company leader and so on to ordinary families barely making a living. When house prices soar at unprecedented levels, life becomes challenging, resulting in a greater socio-economic disparity. This sort of phenomenon leads to unequal access to public utilities and services such as education, healthcare and employment, and is associated with higher crime rates, poor health outcomes and lower levels of overall happiness. Mumbai — the most populous city of India — is a great example in this scenario, where millions live in poor conditions, resulting in higher crime incidence and overall poor cityscape.

In conclusion, it is beneficial to move to megacities as people can access to numerous choices and opportunities, yet these are overshadowed by issues like overpopulation, environmental damage, and increased costs of accommodation. Therefore, I believe urbanization of metropolians is a quite negative trend.

question: Nowadays, young people admire media and sports stars, even though they do not set a good example. Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
content:
Famous people usually have a huge influence on people, especially young people whether it is positive or negative, and there is a view that celebrities on media and in sports are looked up to by these young fans, whereas their impact is considered negative. This is mainly due to their unhealthy behavior, yet I assume that there are also favorable sides like intrinsic motivation and foreign culture exposure.

We cannot say famous people on the internet and in sports are great examples, for they embody toxic behavior in their actions oftentimes. These people can promote violence, adult related stuff like drinking and smoking in their videos and social media pages, thus setting views in children that these sorts of actions are totally rational, whereby this leads to poor lifestyle choices in children's life. Eventually, those who are effected by this in the long run can create a society of emotionally and mentally ill citizens. For instance, now we can observe a mass number of children imitating recklessly to social media so called idols, while their actions serve no purpose to the benefit of children.

Having said that, sports and social media idols do have qualities that can help children. Firstly, it is true that most of these figures these fields are self-made and in fact worked hard to achieve to the level now they stand, and their glorious stories of success are able to drive children to chase their dreams and lock in goals they might have set. Muhammad Ali — a worldwide known boxing champion and pioneer of the participation of mixed races in sports- is the great role model to not thousands but millions of the youth, and his stories to the successful path in sports have motivated many.

Apart from serving as an intrinsic motivation, through the internet young generation can be exposed to global culture, familiarizing themselves with diverse cultures. They can watch short videos on social media of these famous people and engage with international celebrities online, resulting in broader worldview and modern awareness. Take young language learners, who learn, say, English through celebrity interviews, while they also journey through cultural differences, becoming more aware of surrounding world.

To conclude, aside from having a negative influence through their harmful image, media and sports stars can actually bring about several advantages to the table such as being an inspiration and helping to break cultural barriers to the youth. Therefore, it is legit to say that admiration towards these figures is promising.

question: The media should include more stories which report good news. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
The outlook of people is mostly shaped by what news they read, and this does effect their daily life. With this fact, there is a view that more stories with good news covered should be shown by the media, such as radio, TV shows and newspapers. I admit that this is going to help nourish the spirits, yet I oppose to this idea for two main reasons.

One of the most common supports towards ‘only good news’ trend is the measure taken to build physiological resilience. Oftentimes people who are exposed to negative narratives constantly see decreases in their emotional state - for example, declined stability and nurturing of chronic anxiety. This can be explained by the fact that a news environment dominated by uplifting stories reduce cognitive overload and emotional fatigue;as a result, there might be more communities with higher levels of optimism, hope, and emotional endurance, whose psychology becomes more resilient too, and increased productiveness and cooperation signs can be also observed. Plus, these people initiate being forward-looking towards their long-term lives. During national recovery periods after natural disasters or wars, countries, highlighting stories of rebuilding and cooperativeness, often exhibit faster community healing and volunteer engagement, for instance.

With that being said, I mainly put emphasis on the encouragement of negative news. Firstly, it leads to increased informed civic awareness. People - in order to solve issues within societies - should be exposed to some harsh truths of their environment rather than just negating them. This is important because reporting unpleasant truths about injustice, corruption and systematic failure urges people to gain knowledge necessary to demand accountability and reform, where awareness becomes the foundation of collective power and civic participation towards common societal problems instead of passive consumption. Therefore, we have investigative journalism which reveals unsafe working conditions, issues in some regions and corruption within governments sectors, leading eventually to the development of societies.

Further, negative narratives bring people to realistic world comprehension. This is mainly because positive ones usually distort reality and intellectual complacency, while exposure to the former helps to train some intrinsic traits such as critical thinking and emotional maturity. People start to see the world at much bigger pictures and develop resilience made of realism, not just illusion,say, this can prevent public shock to an unexpected rise of societal issues, dealing with it in a strategic approach. Take news aggregators which report about economic downturns - they help families and households to plan in advance, adapt, and mitigate long-term damage.

In conclusion, it is true that prolonged exposure to negative news often do harm than good, where positive news can build emotionally resilient community;however, it is even more important to ensure public awareness about available problems and foster realistic world horizons.

question: The values we learn from our parents and family have a greater influence on our success than the knowledge and the skills we learn at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
content:
It is believed that the influence acquired from parents in terms of social and moral values cannot be replaced by knowledge and skills learned at school.This idea does have its own perks like moral values, yet I primarily oppose to this notion as the school can have more to offer to children beyond basic subject-related knowledge.

One of the most intrinsic treats parents can teach to children is the range of values related to real-life, ranging from accountability to honesty. Parents are considered to be the initial teachers of children since the day they are born ,and children learn how to walk, communicate with the outside world and speak from parents - skills that are fundamental in life. The best example scenario can be in this regard when fathers introduce their children into the responsibility of being a man of the house, taking care of family members and doing households tasks like fixing and protecting, while mothers often resemble a role of teachers who can show what is honesty and compassion towards other people. These traits cannot be easily gained throughout a short term and often is not included in the school curriculum.

On the other hand, I assert that the role of the school in children’s development remains fundamentally irreplaceable. First of all, we need to take into account that school oftentimes can confer access to specialized knowledge and intellectual capital, which are intrinsic for the future career. From the day we start attending classrooms, diverse subjects at school teach us academic knowledge needed to excel in one profession, while these lessons also can boost one’s creativity, leading to the acquisition of market-relevant expertise and professional specialization, results of which are enhanced employability, upward career mobility and economic opportunity creation. For instance, most countries are now encouraging the STEM education - the specific system focusing on building on career-relevant skills - which proves to be of high importance, and in fact, such aforementioned advantages of conventional education is not easily gained through only parental teachings.

Another primary difference of school education from familial training is the development of social skills and collaborative competence. In most school settings, children can interact with their peers, work on team projects and be exposed to institutional social environments;as a result, they can cultivate communication skills, leadership capacity and intercultural awareness - in cases, when the school comprise students from different backgrounds. Individuals, once have been in such surroundings, can adopt greater adaptability in complex workplaces and network-based success pathways. Take debate clubs - provided in almost every classrooms - where students work in pairs or groups, and they can attain high-level speaking and argumentation skills far beyond everyday conversations as debates require participants to think critically and organize ideas coherently.

In conclusion, it is undeniable that there is a foundational role of parents in children’s development by instilling real-life values, but school education remains indispensable because it not only provides specialized knowledge, but also does it develop social skills.

question: In many parts of the world, children are given more freedom than in the past. Is this a positive or negative development?
content:
From tightly-regulated households to increasingly liberal upbringings, the shift in how children are raised has changed quite considerably, with one of such changes being increased freedom given to children around the globe. There are rational explanations to why this trend is happening, yet it is undesirable change as a whole.

There are several significant perks to more freedom children have now. Firstly, it can boost overall self-confidence of children. When parents give an opportunity to their children to make choices in life - for instance, choosing the university course or hobbies - it fosters self-learning and responsibility within children. These qualities are crucial for personality formation, helping children express themselves freely, where gradually granting freedoms nurtures trust between parents and children, effectively reducing rebellion and risky behaviours. Take a scenario when a child has to pick a certain club at school: by making introducing themselves to different activities they may get a picture of what their capabilities are.

With that being said, greater autonomy in children's life can entail negative impact - for instance, a lack of discipline and weakened parental guidance. The latter usually occurs when there is too much independence in terms of some important daily choices, such as habits, values and friends, Given excessive freedom, a child can adopt toxic habits like smoking or overplaying games. Long term effects of these are oftentimes too detrimental, leading to failure in academic standards and poor self-control. Children, for instance, spend too much hours on social media rather than do their coursework in most of the families because there can be no parental guidance in some households.

Culture is another aspect of life that can incur a risk from increased autonomy. When the structure is absent and parents use permissive approach to parenting, traditional bonds, once taught children shared values and collective responsibility in a family, might be loosened. In such situations, young children can prioritize personal preference over communal duty, treating household rules as optional.and neglecting advice of elderly. At first glance, this appears to signal healthy growth; yet beneath the surface, it can gradually break the moral frame that sustains family cohesion. Over time, this shift may weaken moral senses in a family, such as respect, gratitude, and obligation, replacing it with a more individualistic mindset, a transformation that reshapes cultural values.

In conclusion, greater independence makes room for improvement for children like gaining confidence, although it mostly speaks to unfavorable changes in the family cohesion like the lost of cultural morals and detrimental behavioural transformations in children.

question: In schools and universities, girls tend to choose arts while boys like science. What are the reasons for this trend and do you think this tendency should be changed?
content:
There are certainly some gender specific preferences towards different things in life, and it is well-known that female students lean more towards arts, whilst it is more common for males to choose science in educational institutions such as schools and universities. Reasons like cultural stereotypes and childhood toys correlate with this shift, while I assume that there should be attempts to encourage both boys and girls to opposite fields.

First of all, the main reason why there is an interest disparity in institutions is because of conventional views. These views oftentimes claim that females are relatively more creative, and males are more capable of doing problem-solving skills. Even, during many centuries there were more female artists, singers, performers and professionals who fall in such category, while it is no mystery that many of the scientists were males. This figures also contribute to modern choices of people, where girls at school, often looking up to historic figures of their gender, opt to pursue education in arts - the reverse trend is observed for males.

Further, since childhood years, we tend to shape the educational preferences of children through what sorts of toys they are exposed to. Boys at their early years more engage in playing with toys that challenge cognitive skills like problem solving, critical thinking, leadership, and decision making - for instance, puzzle games or the well-known Lego construction toys. question: It is believed that people are celebrating common holidays increasingly with less interest such as New Year. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Holiday celebrations have always been of a huge importance among people, yet there is a view that this tradition is becoming less popular among people such as during the New Year holiday. I partially agree to this view due to two reasons, while I acknowledge that nothing has changed.

Admittedly, there is no change in terms of holiday celebrations at all .
